definition_zh: 成年人；成年动物或成株植物；法定成年人；成年的；供成人使用的；举止成熟的
definition_en: a fully grown person or animal, or something that is fully grown, intended for grown people, or behaving in a mature way
core_image: 褪去稚气的身影：肩膀长开、步子变稳，能独自担起一件事
scene: 毕业典礼结束后，家长们陆续走进礼堂，各自找位置坐下。Every adult in the hall received a copy of the school report.
sceneCN: 这里 adult 是「成年人」（第 1 个义项：身体发育完全的成年人类）；句意为礼堂里每位成年人都拿到了一份学校报告。

pos.zh: 名词：成年人；成年动物；法律意义上的成年人
形容词：成年的；供成人使用的；举止成熟的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -hood 构成，义为「成年期；成年身份」
由本词加后缀 -ing 构成，口语指「像成年人一样独立生活、承担责任」
由本词加形容词后缀 -like 构成，义为「像成年人一样的」

senses.title: A fully grown person
senses.definition: a human being who has reached full physical growth and is no longer a child
senses.definitionCN: 身体发育完全、已不再是儿童的人
senses.example: One adult must accompany each group of children.
senses.exampleCN: 每组孩子都必须有一名成年人陪同。
senses.why: Latin adultus is the past participle of adolescere, to grow up, so the word names the person in whom growth is already finished.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adultus 是 adolescere「长大」的过去分词，因此这个词指「成长已经完成」的人。

senses.title: A fully developed animal or plant
senses.definition: an animal or plant that has reached its full size and is able to reproduce
senses.definitionCN: 长到完整大小、具备繁殖能力的动物或植物
senses.example: The adult moth has no mouth and lives only a few days.
senses.exampleCN: 成年飞蛾没有口器，只能活几天。
senses.why: The idea of finished growth belongs to every living thing, not only to people, so the noun extends to the whole living world.
senses.whyCN: 「生长完成」的念头属于一切生物而不只属于人，于是名词扩展到整个生物界。

senses.title: A person of legal age
senses.definition: a person who has reached the age at which the law grants full rights and duties
senses.definitionCN: 已达到法律赋予完全权利与义务的年龄的人
senses.example: In this country a citizen is a legal adult at eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个国家，公民年满十八岁即为法定成年人。
senses.why: Nature sets no exact date, so the law fixes one; a grown body is then recognised by an age written into a statute.
senses.whyCN: 自然没有给出确切日期，于是法律定出一个；长成的身体由此被写进法条的那个年龄确认。

senses.title: Fully grown, as an adjective
senses.definition: having reached full size or maturity and no longer young
senses.definitionCN: 已达到完整大小或成熟状态、不再幼小的
senses.example: An adult oak can stand thirty metres tall.
senses.exampleCN: 一棵成年橡树可以长到三十米高。
senses.why: The adjective simply labels the state that the noun names; nothing is added except the grammatical role.
senses.whyCN: 形容词只是给名词所指的状态贴上标签，除了语法角色之外没有增添任何东西。

senses.title: Intended for grown people only
senses.definition: describing films, books or other material meant for grown people, often because of sex or violence
senses.definitionCN: 形容电影、书刊等只供成年人接触的内容，常因涉及性画面或暴力
senses.example: The shop keeps adult magazines on a shelf behind the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店把成人杂志放在柜台后面的架子上。
senses.why: Grown people are the intended audience, so the word draws a line at the entrance and marks who may pass.
senses.whyCN: 成年人是预设的读者，于是这个词在入口处划出一条界线，标明谁可以进去。

senses.title: Mature in behaviour
senses.definition: sensible and responsible in the way a grown person is expected to be
senses.definitionCN: 像成年人那样明智、负责任的
senses.example: She gave an adult answer instead of blaming the others.
senses.exampleCN: 她给出了一个成熟的回答，而不是责怪别人。
senses.why: Growth moves from the body to the temper: someone whose reactions are no longer childish is called adult.
senses.whyCN: 「生长」从身体转移到性情：一个反应不再幼稚的人就被称为 adult。

intro.en: Adult is a Latin past participle taken into English almost unchanged; the whole family circles around the verb for growing up.
intro.cn: adult 是一个几乎原样进入英语的拉丁语过去分词；整个词族都围绕「长大」这个动词。

items.en: The verb alescere meant to grow; it is an inchoative form built on alere, to nourish. The deeper Indo-European source is not certain.
items.cn: 动词 alescere 意为「生长」，是由 alere「滋养」构成的起始动词；更早的印欧语来源不确定。

items.en: Ad plus alescere gave adolescere, to grow up, the verb behind both adolescent and adolescence.
items.cn: ad- 与 alescere 合成 adolescere「长大」，adolescent 与 adolescence 都出自这个动词。

items.en: The past participle adultus meant having grown up, full grown; Latin already applied it to people and to animals.
items.cn: 过去分词 adultus 意为「已长成的、发育完全的」；拉丁语已经用它指人，也指动物。

items.en: English borrowed adult directly from Latin in the mid seventeenth century rather than through French. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪中叶直接从拉丁语借入 adult，并未经由法语；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The legal and entertainment senses came later: statutes needed a fixed age, and cinemas needed a label for restricted material.
items.cn: 法律义与影娱义是后来的延伸：法条需要固定年龄，影院需要给受限内容贴标签。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the growth family around adolescere; the near-meaning group gathers words for grown people and their opposite.
note.cn: 形近组收围绕 adolescere 的「生长」词族；近义组收指称成年人的词及其反义对照。

entries.definition: The period of life between childhood and adulthood, built on the same Latin verb as adult.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春期」，指童年与成年之间的时期，与 adult 同出拉丁语 adolescere。

entries.definition: A young person between child and adult, or the adjective describing that stage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「青少年」或「青春期的」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: The state or period of being an adult, formed directly from adult plus -hood.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年期」，由 adult 加后缀 -hood 直接构成。

entries.definition: An adult, used especially by or to children; warmer and less formal than adult.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「大人、成年的」，多用于儿童语境，比 adult 更亲切、更口语。

entries.definition: Fully developed or sensible; it stresses emotional readiness rather than age.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「成熟的」，强调心理上的准备而非年龄。

entries.definition: A person below the legal age of adulthood, the legal opposite of an adult.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「未成年人」，是法定成年人的法律反义。

entries.definition: A young human being who has not yet reached adulthood.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「儿童」，指尚未成年的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin growth root and the common phrases adult actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁「生长」词根，以及 adult 实际构成的常见搭配。

normal.en: Adolescere is to grow up; adultus is its past participle, having grown.
normal.cn: adolescere 意为「长大」；adultus 是它的过去分词，意为「已经长成」。

normal.en: Adolescence, adolescent and adult all come from the same verb alescere.
normal.cn: adolescence、adolescent 与 adult 都出自同一个动词 alescere。

normal.en: Adulthood is adult plus -hood, the state of being grown.
normal.cn: adulthood 是 adult 加 -hood，即「已长成」的状态。

normal.en: Adult education means classes for people who are past ordinary school age.
normal.cn: adult education 指为过了普通学龄的人开设的课程。

normal.en: A young adult is already grown but still in the early part of adult life.
normal.cn: young adult 指已经成年、但仍处在成年生活早期的人。

abstract.en: Picture a sapling whose trunk has finally hardened: the rings are complete and it no longer bends at a touch.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树苗的树干终于变硬：年轮已经长满，再轻轻一碰也不会弯。

abstract.en: The same trunk can become a ticket at a cinema door, where adult marks who is old enough to enter.
abstract.cn: 同一根树干也可以变成影院门口的一张票，adult 在那里标明谁够年龄进场。

abstract.en: A grown body and a grown temper are two rings of the same tree.
abstract.cn: 长成的身体与长成的性情，是同一棵树上的两圈年轮。

examples.en: Only adults may enter this exhibition.
examples.cn: 只有成年人才能进入这个展览。

examples.en: The adult bear weighs twice as much as its cub.
examples.cn: 成年熊的体重是幼崽的两倍。

examples.en: She gave an adult answer instead of looking for someone to blame.
examples.cn: 她给出了成熟的回答，而不是去找人背锅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿达特」——阿达终于长大，说话做事都有了分寸：成年人

root: 拉丁语 adultus 是 adolescere「长大」的过去分词，由 ad-「朝向」+ alescere「生长」构成，字面意思是「已经长成的」；alescere 又由 alere「滋养」派生。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of adult all rest on one image, growth finished: a grown person, a grown animal, the age the law fixes, the adjective for full size, material meant for grown people, and behaviour that has stopped being childish.
sensesIntro.cn: adult 的六个义项都建立在同一个意象「生长完成」上：长成的人、长成的动物、法律定下的年龄、表示完整大小的形容词、只供成年人接触的内容，以及不再幼稚的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sapling has grown into a trunk whose rings are complete and whose bark no longer gives way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵树苗长成了树干，年轮已经长满，树皮也不再一碰就陷。

branches.en: THE BODY: growth is finished, and the person can now stand alone.
branches.cn: 身体线：生长完成，人从此可以独自站稳。

branches.en: THE SPECIES: the same finished growth describes animals and plants that can reproduce.
branches.cn: 物种线：同样的「生长完成」也用来描述能繁殖的动物和植物。

branches.en: THE STATUTE: the law turns a biological state into a fixed birthday.
branches.cn: 法条线：法律把一种生理状态变成一个固定的生日。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the adjective names the completed state and adds nothing else.
branches.cn: 标签线：形容词只命名完成的状态，不再添加别的意思。

branches.en: THE DOOR AND THE TEMPER: grown people are the audience of restricted material, while maturity of behaviour is growth turned inward.
branches.cn: 门槛与性情线：成年人是受限内容的观众，而举止的成熟则是「生长」转向内心。

intro.en: Adult is a Latin participle used unchanged in English; its family grows by ordinary English suffixes.
intro.cn: adult 是一个原样借入英语的拉丁语过去分词；它的词族靠普通英语后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Adolescere and adultus are both recorded Latin forms, so nothing in this list has to be reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: adolescere 与 adultus 都是有文献记录的拉丁语形式，因此这里没有需要重构的部分。

items.example: The prefix directs growth towards its end.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「生长」引向终点。

items.example: The root carries the idea of growth itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载「生长」本身的观念。

items.example: English took the participle as it stood.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个分词原样借了过来。

items.example: The participle of the same verb named a stage of life.
items.exampleCN: 同一动词的分词变成了人生的一个阶段。

items.meaning: the state of being an adult
items.example: It joins adult to the suffix -hood.
items.exampleCN: 它把 adult 与后缀 -hood 结合起来。
它由 adult 构成 adulthood。

items.example: It forms adulting in informal use.
Publishers label this age group with the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 出版方用这个短语标注这一年龄段的读者。

latinEntries.meaning: youth, the age of growing up

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -hood 构成，义为「成年期；成年身份」
由本词加后缀 -ing 构成，口语指「像成年人一样独立生活、承担责任」
由本词加形容词后缀 -like 构成，义为「像成年人一样的」

definition_zh: 前进；推进；促进；提前；预付；晋升；提出（观点）；进展；上涨
definition_en: to move forward, to help something make progress, to move an event to an earlier time, or to put forward an idea; as a noun, forward progress or an increase
core_image: 棋盘上一枚棋子被推到更靠前的格子，局面随之前移
scene: 雨季里，队伍沿着泥泞的山路一点点向前挪动。The rescue team advanced along the muddy trail before sunrise.
sceneCN: 这里 advance 是「前进」（第 1 个义项：向更靠前的位置移动）；句意为救援队在日出前沿着泥泞的小径向前推进。

pos.zh: 不及物动词：前进；进展；上涨
及物动词：推进；提前；预付；晋升；提出
名词：进展；前进；预付款；价格上涨

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「推进；提升；进展」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「先进的；高级的；晚期的」

senses.title: To move forward
senses.definition: to move to a position further forward, especially with a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 向更靠前的位置移动，尤指有目的地移动
senses.example: The column advanced through the pass before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍在黎明前穿过山口向前推进。
senses.why: Late Latin abante meant from before, so the word already contains the picture of the ground in front; the first sense is simply a body or a troop moving into it.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 abante 意为「从前面」，词里先有「前方那块地面」的画面；第一个义项就是人或军队移进那块地面。

senses.title: To help something make progress
senses.definition: to help a plan, cause or process move forward faster or more effectively
senses.definitionCN: 帮助计划、事业或进程更快、更有效地向前发展
senses.example: The loan advanced the building work by several months.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔贷款把工程向前推进了好几个月。
senses.why: The same forward movement is applied to something that cannot walk; a cause is pushed along instead of a person.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「向前」被用在不会走路的事物上：被推着走的不是人，而是一项事业。

senses.title: To move an event to an earlier time
senses.definition: to change the date or time of an event so that it happens sooner
senses.definitionCN: 把活动的时间或日期改早，使其更早发生
senses.example: The committee advanced the meeting from Friday to Tuesday.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会把会议从周五提前到周二。
senses.why: On a calendar what lies further in front is sooner, so pushing an event forward means moving it to an earlier day.
senses.whyCN: 在日历上越靠前就越早，因此把活动「往前推」就是把日期挪到更早的一天。

senses.title: To pay money before it is due
senses.definition: to pay or lend money before the work is done or before the normal time of payment
senses.definitionCN: 在工作完成之前或正常付款时间之前支付或借出钱款
senses.example: The publisher advanced her a sum against future royalties.
senses.exampleCN: 出版商按未来版税预支给她一笔钱。
senses.why: Money handed over ahead of its normal date is literally paid in advance, and the noun advance names that sum.
senses.whyCN: 在正常日期之前交出去的钱正是「提前」支付的，名词 advance 指的就是这笔预付款。

senses.title: To raise someone to a higher rank
senses.definition: to move a person to a higher position or rank
senses.definitionCN: 把人提升到更高的职位或级别
senses.example: After the campaign he was advanced to the rank of captain.
senses.exampleCN: 战役之后他被晋升为上尉。
senses.why: Upward and forward are one gesture: the person is moved to a square nearer the top of the board.
senses.whyCN: 向上与向前是同一个动作：人被挪到更靠近棋盘顶端的一格。

senses.title: To put forward an idea
senses.definition: to suggest or present an idea, theory or plan for others to consider
senses.definitionCN: 提出想法、理论或计划供他人考虑
senses.example: She advanced a simple explanation for the sudden drop in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 她对销量骤降提出了一个简单的解释。
senses.why: An idea is pushed out in front of the group, where everyone can see it and argue about it.
senses.whyCN: 想法被推到人群前面，好让每个人都能看见并讨论。

senses.title: Forward progress or a rise
senses.definition: the progress already made, or a rise in price, value or amount
senses.definitionCN: 已经取得的进展，或价格、价值、数量的上涨
senses.example: The report recorded a steady advance in reading scores.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录到阅读成绩的稳步提升。
senses.why: The noun measures the distance covered by the same forward move, whether the ground is a project or a price.
senses.whyCN: 名词衡量的是同一次「向前」覆盖了多少距离，无论那片地面是一个项目还是一项价格。

intro.en: Advance reaches English through Old French, and the whole family is anchored in the Latin words for before and in front.
intro.cn: advance 经由古法语进入英语，整个词族都锚定在拉丁语表示「在前」的词上。

items.en: Ante is the Latin preposition and adverb for before, in front of, and it anchors the whole family.
items.cn: ante 是拉丁语介词与副词，意为「在……之前、在前面」，是整个词族的锚点。

items.en: Late Latin abante combined ab, from, with ante, before, giving the sense from before, in front.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 abante 把 ab「从」与 ante「前」合并，形成「从前面、在前方」的意思。

items.en: Old French avancier meant to move forward and to put forward; the same family gave avant, before.
items.cn: 古法语 avancier 意为「向前移动、推进」，同一词族还生出 avant「在前」。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English in the fifteenth century and the noun follows in the sixteenth. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 动词在十五世纪见于英语记录，名词随后在十六世纪出现；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The commercial senses split off later: an advance can now be money paid early, a price rise, or a proposal put to a committee.
items.cn: 商业义后来分化：advance 现在可以指提前支付的钱、价格的上涨，或提交给委员会的建议。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the avant family; the near-meaning group gathers other words for going onward, helping, or moving back.
note.cn: 形近组收 avant 词族；近义组收其他表示前行、助推或后退的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of moving something forward or the promotion that results.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「推进；提升」，指推动某事向前的行为或由此获得的晋升。

entries.definition: Carried forward, and therefore higher, later or more developed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「先进的；高级的；晚期的」，即被「推到前面」的状态。

entries.definition: A position in front of others, built on the same avant root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优势」，即站在别人前面的位置，与 advance 同出 avant 词根。

entries.definition: Forward movement towards a goal; the noun stresses the ground already covered.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进步、进展」，强调已经走过的距离。

entries.definition: To continue or move onward, often after a pause.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「继续进行、前行」，常指停顿之后继续。

entries.definition: To help something grow or to raise someone in rank, covering senses two and five.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「促进；提升」，可对应本词第 2 与第 5 个义项。

entries.definition: To move backwards away from danger, the reverse of advancing.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「撤退」，与「前进」方向相反。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin words for before and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「在前」类词语，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Abante is ab plus ante: the word starts from the position already in front.
normal.cn: abante 是 ab 加 ante：这个词从「已经在前方」的位置起步。

normal.en: Advance, advantage and advancement all descend from avant, before.
normal.cn: advance、advantage 与 advancement 都出自 avant「在前」。

normal.en: In advance means before the fixed time, which is why the money sense and the date sense meet there.
normal.cn: in advance 意为在约定时间之前，付款义与日期义正是在这里交汇。

normal.en: An advance on a salary is money paid ahead of the work.
normal.cn: 工资的 advance 就是在工作完成之前先付的那笔钱。

normal.en: Advanced work is work that has been carried further forward than the rest.
normal.cn: advanced 的工作就是被推得比其余部分更靠前的工作。

abstract.en: Picture a chess piece lifted and set on the next square: the board does not change, only the position does.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚棋子被拿起，放到前面一格：棋盘没变，变的是位置。

abstract.en: The same hand can move a clock to an earlier hour or a soldier up a rank; both are one forward gesture.
abstract.cn: 同一只手可以把时钟拨到更早的时刻，也可以把士兵提到更高的级别；两者都是同一个「向前」的手势。

abstract.en: A theory is a card pushed to the middle of the table so that everyone can read it.
abstract.cn: 理论就是一张被推到桌子中央、让所有人都能读到的卡片。

examples.en: Technology advances faster than the rules that govern it.
examples.cn: 技术比约束它的规则进步得更快。

examples.en: They agreed to advance the deadline by a week.
examples.cn: 他们同意把截止日期提前一周。

examples.en: In advance of the storm, the village stored extra water.
examples.cn: 暴风雨来临之前，村子里多存了水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿万斯」——阿万把棋子往前一推，队伍就向前挪了一格：前进

root: 古法语 avancier 出自晚期拉丁语 abante「从前面」，由 ab「从」+ ante「前」构成；字面意思是「从前面来、往前去」，后来分化出前进、推进、预付、晋升等义。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses of advance all describe one forward move applied to different grounds: a body, a cause, a calendar, a purse, a rank, an idea, and the measured result.
sensesIntro.cn: advance 的七个义项都是同一次「向前移动」落在不同的地面上：身体、事业、日历、钱包、职位、想法，以及量出来的结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chess piece is lifted and set on the next square; the ground stays, the position moves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚棋子被拿起放到前面一格；地面不变，位置前移。

branches.en: THE BODY: a person or a troop occupies the ground in front.
branches.cn: 身体线：人或队伍占住了前方那块地面。

branches.en: THE CAUSE AND THE MEASURE: a plan is pushed along, and the noun measures how far it went.
branches.cn: 事业与度量线：计划被推着走，名词则量出它走了多远。

branches.en: THE CLOCK AND THE PURSE: forward on a calendar is sooner, forward in payment is money first.
branches.cn: 时钟与钱包线：日历上的「前」就是更早，付款上的「前」就是先付钱。

branches.en: THE LADDER: the same gesture moves a person up a rank.
branches.cn: 阶梯线：同一个手势把人往上提了一级。

branches.en: THE TABLE: an idea is set in front of the group so that it can be examined.
branches.cn: 桌面线：想法被摆到众人前面，供大家审视。

intro.en: Advance is built from Latin before-words plus an Old French verb, with English suffixes finishing the family.
intro.cn: advance 由拉丁语的「在前」类词加一个古法语动词构成，再由英语后缀补齐词族。

latinIntro.en: Ante, ab and abante are all recorded Latin forms; the Old French verb avancier is also attested, so only the Indo-European layer is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: ante、ab 与 abante 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，古法语动词 avancier 也有文献，只有印欧语层面属于重构。

items.example: It marks the starting point of the movement.
items.exampleCN: 它标出这一移动的起点。

items.example: The word places the goal ahead of the mover.
items.exampleCN: 这个词把目标放在移动者的前方。

items.example: The adverb joined the two Latin pieces.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词把两个拉丁语成分合并起来。

items.example: It is the plain ancestor of advance.
items.exampleCN: 它是 advance 的直接祖先。

items.example: English took this verb as advance.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个动词借作 advance。

items.example: The word serves as both verb and noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词既作动词也作名词。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「推进；提升；进展」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「先进的；高级的；晚期的」

definition_zh: 优势；有利条件；好处；利益；（短语中）利用、占便宜；（网球）占先分
definition_en: a condition or quality that puts someone in a better position than others, or a benefit gained from using something
core_image: 起跑线上，一方的脚已经抢先踏出半步
scene: 比赛开始前，两队站在同一条线上，其中一队的主力已经提前热身。Their early training gave them a clear advantage in the second half.
sceneCN: 这里 advantage 是「优势」（第 1 个义项：使自己处于比别人更有利位置的特质）；句意为提前的训练让他们在下半场拥有明显的优势。

pos.zh: 名词：优势；有利条件；好处；网球占先分

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，义为「有利的；有益的」
由本词加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「不利条件；劣势」
由 advantageous 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「有利地；便利地」

senses.title: A quality that puts you ahead
senses.definition: a quality, skill or asset that places someone in a better position than others
senses.definitionCN: 使人处于比别人更有利位置的特质、技能或资源
senses.example: Her fluency in three languages gave her an advantage at the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她流利掌握三门语言，这让她在面试中占了优势。
senses.why: Old French avantage meant the position in front, so a personal quality is imagined as a foot placed ahead of the others.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 avantage 本指「前面的位置」，因此个人的长处被想象成一只抢先踏出去的脚。

senses.title: A favourable circumstance
senses.definition: a circumstance of place, time or situation that works in someone's favour
senses.definitionCN: 在场所、时间或处境上对某人有利的条件
senses.example: The team lost the advantage of playing at home when the stadium flooded.
senses.exampleCN: 体育场被淹后，球队失去了主场作战的有利条件。
senses.why: Here the foot in front is not a skill but the ground itself: a home pitch or a calm market puts you a step forward.
senses.whyCN: 这里抢先的脚不是技能，而是地面本身：主场或平稳的市场把你往前送了一步。

senses.title: A benefit or profit
senses.definition: a gain or profit that comes from doing or using something
senses.definitionCN: 因做某事或使用某物而得到的好处或利益
senses.example: The seller explained what advantage the buyer would gain from the larger order.
senses.exampleCN: 卖家说明了更大的订单会给买方带来什么好处。
senses.why: The forward position is turned into something you take: the advantage becomes a measurable gain.
senses.whyCN: 「前面的位置」被转化成可以拿到的东西：优势变成了可衡量的收益。

senses.title: To exploit, in the phrase take advantage of
senses.definition: in the phrase take advantage of, to use someone or something for one's own gain, sometimes unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 take advantage of，指为自身利益利用某人或某物，有时带有不公平意味
senses.example: He took advantage of her kindness and borrowed money he never returned.
senses.exampleCN: 他利用她的善良借了钱，却一直没还。
senses.why: If an advantage is a step in front, taking advantage of someone is stepping over them to get there.
senses.whyCN: 如果 advantage 是抢先的一步，那么 take advantage of 某人就是踩着对方抢先过去。

senses.title: The point after deuce in tennis
senses.definition: the point scored after deuce that gives a player one point more than the opponent and the chance to win the game
senses.definitionCN: 平分之后得到的一分，使球员比对手多一分并取得赢下这一局的机会
senses.example: At advantage, the server needed only one more point to win the game.
senses.exampleCN: 到了占先，发球方只再拿一分就能赢下这一局。
senses.why: Tennis named the state by the same picture: one player stands a single point ahead, one step in front of level.
senses.whyCN: 网球用同一幅画面来命名这个状态：一名球员领先一分，站在与平分相比靠前一步的位置。

intro.en: Advantage comes from Old French and keeps the plain meaning of its ancestor avant: the position in front.
intro.cn: advantage 来自古法语，保留了祖先 avant 的基本意思：前面的位置。

items.en: Ante meant before, in front of, and stands at the head of the family.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前、在前面」，处在这个词族的源头。

items.en: Ab plus ante gave abante, from before; the same source produced advance.
items.cn: ab 与 ante 合成 abante「从前面」；advance 也出自同一来源。

items.en: Avant meant before, in front, and is the plain ancestor of both advance and advantage.
items.cn: avant 意为「在前、在……之前」，是 advance 与 advantage 的共同祖先。

items.en: Avantage named the position in front, and from that came superiority, a favourable circumstance and a gain.
items.cn: avantage 本指「前面的位置」，由此发展出优势、有利条件与好处。

items.en: Advantage entered English in the fifteenth century; the tennis use is first recorded in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: advantage 于十五世纪进入英语；网球用法最早见于十六世纪。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on avant; the near-meaning group gathers other words for being ahead or for what holds you back.
note.cn: 形近组收由 avant 构成的一族词；近义组收其他表示「领先」或「拖后」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning favourable or giving a benefit, formed from advantage plus -ous.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有利的、有益的」，由 advantage 加 -ous 构成。

entries.definition: An unfavourable condition; the same root with the negative prefix dis-.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不利条件」，是同一词根加否定前缀 dis- 构成。

entries.definition: To move forward; it shares the avant ancestor and the picture of a step in front.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「前进；进展」，与 advantage 同出 avant，共享「抢先一步」的画面。

entries.definition: A good result or profit; it names the gain rather than the position that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「好处、益处」，指所得的结果，而不指产生它的位置。

entries.definition: A small advantage over others; informal and often used of competition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「微弱优势」，口语色彩强，多用于竞争语境。

entries.definition: A special right granted to a person or group, not a positional advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「特权、优待」，指被授予的特殊权利，而非位置上的领先。

entries.definition: A disadvantage or problem that makes something less attractive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺点、不利之处」，是优势的反面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real avant root and the phrases advantage actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 avant 词根，以及 advantage 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Avant means before: advantage is literally the position in front.
normal.cn: avant 意为「在前」：advantage 字面上就是「前面的位置」。

normal.en: Advantage, advance and advantageous all come from the same avant.
normal.cn: advantage、advance 与 advantageous 都出自同一个 avant。

normal.en: Take advantage of keeps the old image: you step in front of someone for your own gain.
normal.cn: take advantage of 保留了旧画面：为了自己的好处，踩到别人前面去。

normal.en: A competitive advantage is one firm standing a step ahead of its rivals.
normal.cn: competitive advantage 就是一家公司比对手多站出一步。

normal.en: In tennis, advantage is the point that puts a player one step ahead of deuce.
normal.cn: 网球里的 advantage 是把球员从平分往前送一步的那一分。

abstract.en: Picture two runners on one line, one with a foot already half a step forward.
abstract.cn: 想象两名跑者站在同一条线上，其中一人已经有一只脚抢先踏出半步。

abstract.en: The same half step can be a better school, a cheaper supplier or a friend in the right office.
abstract.cn: 同样的半步，可以是一所更好的学校、一个更便宜的供应商，或一位在关键部门的朋友。

abstract.en: A half step taken out of someone else's weakness is the darker side of the same image.
abstract.cn: 从别人的弱点上抢出来的半步，是同一幅画面里更暗的一面。

examples.en: Smaller classes are an advantage for young learners.
examples.cn: 小班对年幼的学习者是一种优势。

examples.en: She took advantage of the quiet morning to finish the report.
examples.cn: 她利用安静的清晨把报告写完了。

examples.en: The home side held a narrow advantage at half time.
examples.cn: 半场结束时主队保持着微弱的领先优势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿万替吉」——阿万抢先半步，吉利的事就落在前头：优势

root: 古法语 avantage 出自 avant「在前」，更早可溯至晚期拉丁语 abante「从前面」，由 ab「从」+ ante「前」构成；由「前面的位置」引申出优势、有利条件和好处。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of advantage all keep one picture, a foot placed in front: a personal quality, a favourable circumstance, a gain taken from it, the unfair version of that step, and tennis scoring.
sensesIntro.cn: advantage 的五个义项都保留同一个画面「抢先踏出的一只脚」：个人长处、有利条件、由此拿到的好处、这个动作不公平的一面，以及网球的计分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: on a starting line, one runner's foot is already half a step forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：起跑线上，一名跑者的一只脚已经抢先踏出半步。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a skill or quality is the foot that lands first.
branches.cn: 个人线：技能或长处就是那只先落地的脚。

branches.en: THE GROUND: the surroundings themselves can push one side ahead.
branches.cn: 环境线：场地与时机本身也能把一方往前送。

branches.en: THE PROFIT: the step in front is cashed in as a measurable gain.
branches.cn: 收益线：抢先的一步被兑换成可衡量的好处。

branches.en: THE UNFAIR STEP: the same move made over someone else becomes exploitation.
branches.cn: 失序线：同一个动作踩到别人身上，就变成了利用。

branches.en: THE SCOREBOARD: tennis keeps the picture as one point ahead of level.
branches.cn: 记分线：网球把这幅画面保留为「比平分多一分」。

intro.en: Advantage is Latin-before plus an Old French noun ending; English later added its own prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: advantage 由拉丁语的「在前」类词加古法语名词词尾构成，英语后来又加上自己的前缀与后缀。

latinIntro.en: Ante, ab and abante are attested Latin forms, and avantage is a recorded Old French noun, so no part of the core has to be reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: ante、ab 与 abante 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，avantage 也是有文献的古法语名词，核心部分无需重构。

items.exampleCN: 它带着「从某点移开」的意思。

items.example: It is the link between Latin and French.
items.exampleCN: 它是拉丁语与法语之间的环节。

items.example: Avant is the plain ancestor of this noun.
items.exampleCN: avant 是这个名词的直接祖先。

definition_zh: 冒险；冒险经历；奇遇；冒险活动；有风险的事业
definition_en: an exciting and sometimes dangerous experience, or the spirit of seeking unknown and risky situations
core_image: 背上行囊推开一扇没有门牌的门，外面是没走过的路
scene: 少年把地图折进行囊，站在村口那条从未走过的路上。Their first adventure began at the fork beyond the village.
sceneCN: 这里 adventure 是「冒险经历」（第 1 个义项：令人兴奋又带风险的经历）；句意为他们的第一次冒险是从村外的岔路口开始的。

pos.zh: 名词：冒险；冒险经历；奇遇；风险事业

collocations.zh: 一次有风险的商业尝试

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，义为「爱冒险的；充满惊险的」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「冒险家；投机者」
由 adventurer 加名词后缀 -ism 构成，义为「冒险主义」

senses.title: An exciting and risky experience
senses.definition: an experience that is exciting and involves danger or uncertainty
senses.definitionCN: 令人兴奋、带有危险或不确定性的经历
senses.example: Their trip across the desert became a real adventure when the truck broke down.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车抛锚后，他们横穿沙漠的旅程成了一次真正的冒险。
senses.why: Latin adventura meant the things that are about to happen, so an adventure is first of all an event that comes at you unbidden.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adventura 意为「将要发生的事」，因此 adventure 首先是一件不请自来、迎面发生的事。

senses.title: A strange or remarkable happening
senses.definition: an unusual and striking event or encounter that is remembered and retold
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常、令人难忘并会被讲述的事件或相遇
senses.example: He described his adventure with the stranger on the night train.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲述了他在夜班火车上与那位陌生人的奇遇。
senses.why: When chance events are told as stories, the dangerous edge fades and what remains is the strangeness of what happened.
senses.whyCN: 当偶然事件被当作故事讲述时，危险的一面淡去，留下的是「发生的事」本身的离奇。

senses.title: The seeking of risk and novelty
senses.definition: the activity or spirit of looking for new, unknown and exciting situations
senses.definitionCN: 寻找新的、未知的、刺激的处境的活动或精神
senses.example: She travels for adventure rather than for comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 她旅行是为了寻求冒险，而不是为了舒适。
senses.why: The word shifts from the event to the appetite for it: what comes at you is now something you go out to meet.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「事件」转向「对事件的胃口」：迎面而来的东西，变成了你主动出去迎接的东西。

senses.title: A risky enterprise
senses.definition: an undertaking whose outcome is uncertain and which may bring loss as well as gain
senses.definitionCN: 结果不确定、可能带来损失也可能带来收益的事业
senses.example: The new factory was a costly adventure that few investors supported.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新工厂是一次代价高昂的冒险，支持的投资者寥寥无几。
senses.why: Business borrowed the word for any venture whose result is unknown, keeping the old sense of things about to happen.
senses.whyCN: 商业借用了这个词来指任何结果未知的事业，保留了「将要发生的事」这一旧义。

intro.en: Adventure comes from Latin words for arriving, through Old French; its earliest meaning is simply what is going to happen.
intro.cn: adventure 经由古法语来自拉丁语中表示「到来」的词，最早的意思就是「将要发生的事」。

items.en: Venire meant to come, and it is the moving element in the whole family.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，是整个词族里表示「移动」的成分。

items.en: Ad plus venire gave advenire, to come to, to arrive.
items.cn: ad- 与 venire 合成 advenire，意为「来到、抵达」。

items.en: The future participle produced adventura, the things that are about to happen, a word close to chance and fate.
items.cn: 将来分词构成 adventura，意为「将要发生的事」，接近「偶然」与「命运」。

items.en: Old French aventure meant chance, a happening, an adventure; the sense of a risky undertaking grew in the tales of knights.
items.cn: 古法语 aventure 意为「偶然、事件、冒险」；在骑士故事里逐渐长出「风险事业」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed the word through Anglo-Norman French; the first records are uncertain in date.
items.cn: 英语经由盎格鲁—诺曼法语借入这个词；最早记录的年代不确定。

items.en: The romantic and commercial branches separated: a holiday can be an adventure, and so can a doubtful investment.
items.cn: 浪漫义与商业义逐渐分开：一次度假可以是 adventure，一笔可疑的投资也可以是。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the coming family; the near-meaning group gathers words for journeys and risky undertakings.
note.cn: 形近组收「到来」词族；近义组收表示远行与风险事业的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for someone or something that seeks or contains adventure.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「爱冒险的、充满惊险的」，由 adventure 加 -ous 构成。

entries.definition: A person who seeks adventure, or one who takes risky chances for gain.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冒险家」，也指为获利而投机的人。

entries.definition: A policy or habit of taking reckless risks, usually said with disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冒险主义」，指轻率冒风险的做法，通常带贬义。

entries.definition: An enterprise with an uncertain result; it stresses the money or the project rather than the thrill.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「风险事业、投机」，强调资金或项目本身，而不是刺激感。

entries.definition: An organized journey made for a purpose, such as exploring or research.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「远征、考察」，指有明确目的的成队出行。

entries.definition: A wild, slightly disreputable adventure, usually told with amusement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「越轨的胡闹、荒唐冒险」，讲述时常带调侃意味。

entries.definition: The chance of loss or injury; adventure contains risk but is not defined by it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「风险」，冒险包含风险，但并不等于风险。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb for coming and the phrases adventure actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「来」动词，以及 adventure 实际构成的搭配。

normal.en: Adventura in Latin meant the things that are going to happen.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 adventura 意为「将要发生的事」。

normal.en: Advenire is ad plus venire, to come: an adventure is what comes at you.
normal.cn: advenire 是 ad 加 venire「来」：adventure 就是迎面向你而来的事。

normal.en: Adventure, adventurer and adventurous all keep the coming root.
normal.cn: adventure、adventurer 与 adventurous 都保留了「来」这个词根。

normal.en: A sense of adventure is an appetite for the unknown.
normal.cn: sense of adventure 就是对未知的胃口。

normal.en: An adventure story is built on one unexpected event after another.
normal.cn: adventure story 靠一个接一个的意外事件搭起来。

abstract.en: Picture a door with no number on it, standing at the end of a road you have never walked.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没有门牌的门，立在你从未走过的那条路的尽头。

abstract.en: The same door can be a holiday, a rescue or a factory: what makes it adventure is that nobody knows what is behind it.
abstract.cn: 同一扇门可以是一次度假、一次救援或一座工厂：让它成为冒险的，是没人知道门后是什么。

abstract.en: The pack is light and the map is old, which is why the story begins at the fork.
abstract.cn: 行囊很轻，地图很旧，故事因此从岔路口开始。

examples.en: The climb turned into an adventure when the fog closed in.
examples.cn: 雾气合拢时，那次攀登变成了一场冒险。

examples.en: She has a strong sense of adventure and rarely plans ahead.
examples.cn: 她有很强的冒险精神，很少提前做计划。

examples.en: Their adventures in the mountains filled a whole notebook.
examples.cn: 他们在山中的冒险经历写满了整整一本笔记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿文扯」——阿文扯开地图就往荒野里走：冒险

root: 古法语 aventure 来自拉丁语 adventura「将要发生的事」，是 advenire「到来」的将来分词；ad-「向」+ venire「来」。语义由「偶然发生的事」发展为「冒险经历」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of adventure trace one movement: something comes at you, then you go out to meet it, and finally you stake money on it.
sensesIntro.cn: adventure 的四个义项沿着同一条线：某件事迎面而来，然后你主动出去迎接它，最后你把钱押在它上面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door without a number stands at the end of a road you have never walked.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇没有门牌的门，立在你从未走过的那条路的尽头。

branches.en: THE EXPERIENCE: what comes at you is exciting because it may hurt.
branches.cn: 经历线：迎面而来的事之所以刺激，是因为它可能伤人。

branches.en: THE STORY: once told, the danger becomes the strangeness of the tale.
branches.cn: 故事线：一旦被讲述，危险就变成了故事里的离奇。

branches.en: THE APPETITE: the event turns into something you deliberately go out to find.
branches.cn: 欲望线：事件变成了你特意出去寻找的东西。

branches.en: THE STAKE: an enterprise is an adventure because its outcome is unknown.
branches.cn: 赌注线：一项事业之所以是冒险，因为结果未知。

branches.en: THE TOLD TALE: experience and remarkable happening both survive mainly in the stories people repeat.
branches.cn: 讲述线：冒险经历与奇遇，主要都靠人们反复讲述才留存下来。

intro.en: Adventure joins a Latin prefix of direction to a Latin verb of coming, then passes through Old French before English suffixes attach.
intro.cn: adventure 把拉丁语表方向的副词缀接到表「来」的动词上，再经古法语进入英语，之后才接上英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Venire, advenire and adventura are all attested Latin forms, so only the deeper Indo-European origin is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: venire、advenire 与 adventura 都是有文献的拉丁语形式，只有更早的印欧语来源属于重构。

items.example: It turns coming into coming towards someone.
items.exampleCN: 它把「来」变成「朝某人而来」。
这个动词提供「移动」的意思。

items.example: It is the source of adventure and advent.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adventure 与 advent 的来源。

items.structure: Latin future participle used as a noun
items.example: The participle became a noun of chance.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词变成了表示「偶然」的名词。

items.example: The noun kept the idea of the unforeseen.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词保留了「不可预见」的意思。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

latinEntries.structure: Latin future participle used as a noun

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，义为「爱冒险的；充满惊险的」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「冒险家；投机者」
由 adventurer 加名词后缀 -ism 构成，义为「冒险主义」

definition_zh: 做广告；登广告；宣传；招聘；征求；使引人注意
definition_en: to make goods, services or information known to the public, especially in order to sell or attract attention
core_image: 把一块招牌转向路人，让原本没人留意的东西被看见
scene: 街角的面包店换了新招牌，老板把它搬到路口最显眼的位置。The baker advertised fresh bread on a board outside the door.
sceneCN: 这里 advertise 是「为商品做广告」（第 1 个义项：用公开方式推销商品或服务）；句意为面包师在门外的牌子上宣传新鲜面包。

pos.zh: 及物动词：为……做广告；宣传；招聘；使引人注意
不及物动词：登广告；登广告征求

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「广告；公告」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「广告主；登广告的人」
由本词加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告活动」

senses.title: To promote goods or services publicly
senses.definition: to draw public attention to goods or services, usually by paying for notices, films or posters
senses.definitionCN: 通常通过付费的通告、影片或海报让公众注意商品或服务
senses.example: The firm advertised its new phone on every bus shelter in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在城里每个公交候车亭为它的新手机做广告。
senses.why: Latin advertere is to turn towards: the root image is a sign turned to face the crowd, so people look where they did not look before.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 advertere 意为「转向」：词根的意象是一块被转过来面向人群的招牌，让原本不看的人看过来。

senses.title: To make something widely known
senses.definition: to publicise an event, warning or fact so that many people learn about it
senses.definitionCN: 宣传某个活动、警告或事实，使许多人得知
senses.example: The council advertised the flood warning through local radio.
senses.exampleCN: 市政部门通过本地电台宣传洪水预警。
senses.why: The commercial edge is not needed: anything turned towards the public is announced, whether or not it is for sale.
senses.whyCN: 这里不需要买卖的成分：任何被转向公众的东西都在被「告知」，无论是否出售。

senses.title: To announce a vacancy
senses.definition: to announce a job or post publicly in order to find someone to fill it
senses.definitionCN: 公开公布职位空缺，以便找到合适的人来担任
senses.example: The hospital advertised two nursing posts last week.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院上周登广告招聘两个护理岗位。
senses.why: A vacancy is a notice turned towards possible applicants, so the same verb covers hiring as well as selling.
senses.whyCN: 空缺职位是一张转向潜在申请者的告示，因此同一个动词既能用于卖货，也能用于招人。

senses.title: To ask for someone or something by public notice
senses.definition: to place a notice asking for a person, object or service that one needs
senses.definitionCN: 刊登告示，寻找自己需要的人、物或服务
senses.example: They advertised for a piano teacher in the weekly paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在周报上登广告征求一位钢琴老师。
senses.why: Here the sign faces the other way: instead of offering something, the advertiser is asking the public to come forward.
senses.whyCN: 这里的招牌朝向相反：登广告者不是在提供什么，而是在请公众走上前来。

senses.title: To make something noticeable
senses.definition: to make a quality, fact or presence easy to notice, often unintentionally
senses.definitionCN: 使某种特质、事实或在场状态容易被注意到，常带无意为之的意味
senses.example: He advertised his ignorance by arguing about a language he could not read.
senses.exampleCN: 他争论一种自己看不懂的语言，反而暴露了自己的无知。
senses.why: If advertising is turning attention towards a thing, a person can do it to himself, and the result is usually the opposite of what he wanted.
senses.whyCN: 如果 advertise 是把注意力转向某物，人也可以对自己这么做，而结果往往与他的本意相反。

intro.en: Advertise began as a verb of noticing and informing, and only later acquired its commercial sense.
intro.cn: advertise 起初是一个表示「注意到、告知」的动词，后来才获得商业含义。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, and it is the physical core of the word.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，是这个词的物理核心。

items.en: Ad plus vertere gave advertere, to turn towards something, and therefore to notice it.
items.cn: ad- 与 vertere 合成 advertere，意为「转向某物」，因此引申为「注意到」。

items.en: Old French advertir meant to notice and to inform, keeping both the turning and the telling.
items.cn: 古法语 advertir 兼具「注意到」与「告知」两义，把「转」和「说」都保留下来。

items.en: English first used advertise for noticing and giving notice; the sense of public promotion appears later. Exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语早期用 advertise 表示「注意」与「通知」；公开推广的意思出现得更晚，确切年代不确定。

items.en: The nineteenth-century advertising trade fixed the commercial sense, and the older notice sense survives mainly in formal writing.
items.cn: 十九世纪的广告业固定了商业义，较早的「通告」义主要残存在正式文书里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the vertere family; the near-meaning group gathers words for promoting and announcing.
note.cn: 形近组收 vertere 词族；近义组收表示推广与公布的一类词。

entries.definition: The noun for a public notice, especially a paid one that promotes something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告；公告」，尤指付费的推广性告示，由 advertise 加 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: The person or company that pays for an advertisement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告主、登广告的人」，由 advertise 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The clipped British noun for an advertisement, common in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告」，是 advertisement 的英式截短形式，多见于口语。

entries.definition: To help something sell or become known; broader, and can also mean to raise in rank.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推广、促销」，范围更宽，还可表示「提升职位」。

entries.definition: To make information public; it lacks the selling purpose that advertise usually carries.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣传、公布」，不带 advertise 通常具有的销售目的。

entries.definition: To plan and carry out the selling of a product, as a whole campaign.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「营销」，指把产品销售作为整套活动来策划与执行。

entries.definition: To state something publicly for the first time; it has no advertising intent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣布」，指首次公开说明某事，不带广告意图。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real vertere root and the phrases advertise actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 vertere 词根，以及 advertise 实际构成的搭配。

normal.en: Advertere is ad plus vertere, to turn: advertise turns heads towards a thing.
normal.cn: advertere 是 ad 加 vertere「转」：advertise 就是把头转向某样东西。

normal.en: Advertisement, advertiser and advert all share the same turning root.
normal.cn: advertisement、advertiser 与 advert 都共享同一个「转」的词根。

normal.en: To advertise for someone is to turn the public's eyes towards a wanted post.
normal.cn: advertise for 某人，就是把公众的目光转向一个空缺职位。

normal.en: Heavily advertised goods cost more, because the notice itself has to be paid for.
normal.cn: 广告打得多的商品更贵，因为告示本身是要花钱的。

normal.en: The old sense, to give notice, survives in formal announcements.
normal.cn: 较旧的「发出通知」义，仍残存在正式通告里。

abstract.en: Picture a sandwich board swung round to face the pavement, so that passers-by must look at it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块广告牌被转过来正对人行道，路人不想看都难。

abstract.en: The same board can offer bread, announce a flood or ask for a pianist: the gesture is identical.
abstract.cn: 同一块牌子可以卖面包、发布洪水消息或寻找钢琴手，动作完全一样。

abstract.en: Turned the wrong way, the board shows your own ignorance to everyone.
abstract.cn: 牌子转错了方向，就把你自己的无知展示给了所有人。

examples.en: They advertise their coffee on the radio every morning.
examples.cn: 他们每天早上在电台为自家咖啡做广告。

examples.en: The school advertised for a part-time librarian.
examples.cn: 学校登广告征求一位兼职图书管理员。

examples.en: A well advertised film can still fail at the box office.
examples.cn: 宣传得很好的电影仍可能在票房上失败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德玩太兹」——阿德把招牌转过来，让路人都看见：做广告

root: 古法语 advertir 来自拉丁语 advertere「转向、注意到」，由 ad-「向」+ vertere「转」构成；语义从「使注意」发展为「公开告知」，再到「做广告」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of advertise all perform one gesture, turning something to face the public: selling goods, spreading news, filling a post, asking for help, or exposing oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: advertise 的五个义项都在做同一个动作——把某样东西转向公众：卖货、传消息、补空缺、求帮助，或暴露自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sign is turned round to face the passers-by, who then cannot help noticing it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块招牌被转过来正对路人，路人想不注意都难。

branches.en: THE MARKET: the sign faces buyers and names a price.
branches.cn: 市场线：招牌朝向买家，并标出价钱。

branches.en: THE MEGAPHONE: nothing is sold, but the news still has to reach many ears.
branches.cn: 喇叭线：不卖任何东西，但消息仍要传到许多耳朵里。

branches.en: THE WANTED NOTICE: one notice offers a post, the other asks the public for a person.
branches.cn: 招募线：一张告示提供职位，另一张则请公众提供人选。

branches.en: THE MIRROR: a person turns attention towards himself, usually with an unwanted result.
branches.cn: 镜面线：人把注意力转向自己，结果往往并不如意。

branches.en: THE TURN ITSELF: selling and announcing are the same physical turn, only the content differs.
branches.cn: 转向本身：卖货与告知是同一个物理动作，不同的只是内容。

intro.en: Advertise is a Latin prefix plus a Latin turning verb, reshaped by Old French and then by English suffixes.
intro.cn: advertise 由一个拉丁语前缀加一个表示「转」的拉丁动词构成，经古法语改造后再接英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Vertere and advertere are attested Latin verbs, so the core is recorded rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: vertere 与 advertere 都是有文献的拉丁语动词，核心部分属于有记录的形式而非重构。

items.example: It gives the turning a direction.
The verb is the physical core of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这个词的物理核心。
它把「转」与「注意」连在一起。

items.example: The verb covers both selling and announcing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词兼指卖货与告知。

items.meaning: a public notice or commercial ad

items.example: British speech clips the long noun to advert.
items.exampleCN: 英式口语把长名词截短为 advert。

由本词加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「广告主；登广告的人」

definition_zh: 广告；广告作品；公告；启事；招聘广告；活招牌
definition_en: a public notice, especially a paid one, that promotes a product, service, event or vacancy
core_image: 报纸版面里被框出来的一小块，专门喊住翻页的手
scene: 清晨的地铁车厢里，每个扶手都贴着一张彩色海报。The advertisement above the door promised cheaper train tickets.
sceneCN: 这里 advertisement 是「商业广告」（第 1 个义项：为商品或服务付费刊登的推广告示）；句意为门上方的广告承诺车票会更便宜。

pos.zh: 名词：广告；公告；启事；活招牌

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -ment 回到动词形式，义为「做广告；宣传」
由同族动词 advertise 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「广告主；登广告的人」
由同族动词 advertise 加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告活动」
由本词截短而来，义为「广告」，是英式口语里的简短说法

senses.title: A paid notice promoting goods or services
senses.definition: a notice, film or poster paid for by a seller to persuade people to buy goods or use a service
senses.definitionCN: 卖方付费刊登的通告、影片或海报，用来劝人购买商品或使用服务
senses.example: The advertisement showed a family eating soup around a bright table.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告展示了一家人围坐在明亮的桌旁喝汤。
senses.why: Advertise means to turn attention towards something, and the -ment suffix turns the act into a thing: the turned sign itself.
senses.whyCN: advertise 意为把注意力转向某物，后缀 -ment 把动作变成东西：被转过来的那块招牌本身。

senses.title: A public notice or announcement
senses.definition: a notice that informs the public about an event, a rule or a piece of official information
senses.definitionCN: 向公众说明某个活动、规定或官方信息的告示
senses.example: A small advertisement on the board announced that the library would close early.
senses.exampleCN: 告示板上的一则小启事通知图书馆将提前闭馆。
senses.why: The word was used for any public notice long before shops paid for space, so the informing sense remains beneath the selling one.
senses.whyCN: 在商店付费买版面之前，这个词早已指任何公开告示，因此「告知」这层意思一直留在「销售」之下。

senses.title: A job advertisement
senses.definition: a notice placed by an employer to announce a vacancy and invite applications
senses.definitionCN: 雇主刊登的告示，用来公布职位空缺并征集申请
senses.example: She found the position through a job advertisement in the local paper.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过本地报纸上的一则招聘广告找到了这个职位。
senses.why: An employer turns the notice towards possible applicants instead of buyers, but the object left behind is the same.
senses.whyCN: 雇主把告示转向潜在申请者而不是买家，但留下的那个「东西」仍是同一个。

senses.title: A person or thing that shows something off
senses.titleCN: 活招牌；现身说法的样本
senses.definition: a person or object whose appearance or behaviour openly recommends something
senses.definitionCN: 以外表或行为公开推荐某物的人或物
senses.example: With his sunburn and new boots, he was a walking advertisement for the hiking shop.
senses.exampleCN: 带着晒伤和新靴子，他简直就是那家登山用品店的活招牌。
senses.why: A living body becomes the turned sign: the recommendation is made by being seen rather than by being printed.
senses.whyCN: 活人的身体成了那块被转过来的招牌：推荐靠被人看见完成，而不是靠印在纸上。

intro.en: Advertisement is advertise plus the noun suffix -ment; the base verb came from Latin through Old French.
intro.cn: advertisement 是 advertise 加名词后缀 -ment 构成的；基础动词经由古法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, and the whole family keeps that physical gesture.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，整个词族都保留这个物理动作。

items.en: Advertere meant to turn towards and so to notice; the verb entered French as advertir.
items.cn: advertere 意为「转向」因而「注意到」；这个动词进入法语后作 advertir。

items.en: Old French advertir carried both noticing and informing into English.
items.cn: 古法语 advertir 把「注意」与「告知」两层意思一起带进英语。

items.en: Advertise plus -ment produced advertisement, first meaning a notice or piece of information, not a sales pitch.
items.cn: advertise 加 -ment 构成 advertisement，最初指「通告、消息」，而不是推销词。

items.en: The rise of newspapers and later broadcasting made the commercial sense dominant; the notice sense survives in small print.
items.cn: 报纸乃至广播的兴起使商业义占据主导；「通告」义则残存在小字告示里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the advertise family; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of paid or public notices.
note.cn: 形近组收 advertise 词族；近义组收其他付费或公开的告示类词。

entries.definition: The verb that produces the noun: to promote or make something public.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「做广告；宣传」，是产生这个名词的动词。

entries.definition: The person or firm that pays for the advertisement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告主」，指为广告付费的人或公司。

entries.definition: The clipped British form of advertisement, used mainly in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告」，是 advertisement 的英式截短形式，主要用于口语。

entries.definition: A television or radio advertisement, named after its commercial purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电视或广播广告」，以其商业用途得名。

entries.definition: A campaign or special offer meant to boost sales; broader than one advertisement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「促销活动」，比单则广告的范围更大。

entries.definition: A written statement giving information, without any selling purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「告示、通知」，只提供信息，没有销售目的。

entries.definition: A large outdoor board used to display advertisements.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「户外广告牌」，是张贴广告的大幅板面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real -ment suffix and the phrases advertisement actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的后缀 -ment，以及 advertisement 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Advertisement is advertise plus -ment: the thing left behind by the act.
normal.cn: advertisement 是 advertise 加 -ment：动作完成后留下的那个东西。

normal.en: In the seventeenth century the word meant simply a notice or a piece of information.
normal.cn: 在十七世纪，这个词只表示「通告」或「一条消息」。

normal.en: A job advertisement turns attention towards a vacancy instead of a product.
normal.cn: job advertisement 把注意力转向职位空缺，而不是商品。

normal.en: Advert is the clipped British form of the same long noun.
normal.cn: advert 是同一个长名词在英式口语里的截短形式。

normal.en: A walking advertisement recommends something simply by being seen.
normal.cn: walking advertisement 靠被人看见来推荐某物。

abstract.en: Picture a small boxed square inside a page, reaching out to stop the hand that was about to turn it.
abstract.cn: 想象版面上一个被框起来的小方块，伸出手来拦住正要翻页的那只手。

abstract.en: The same square can sell soup, close a library or hire a nurse; only the message inside changes.
abstract.cn: 同一个小方块可以卖汤、通知闭馆或招聘护士，变的只是里面的字。

abstract.en: Sometimes the box walks out of the page and stands on the street in a new pair of boots.
abstract.cn: 有时这个方块会走出纸面，穿着新靴子站到街上。

examples.en: The advertisement on the wall was almost as tall as the door.
examples.cn: 墙上的那则广告几乎和门一样高。

examples.en: She answered an advertisement for a weekend cook.
examples.cn: 她应征了一则招聘周末厨师的广告。

examples.en: Old newspapers are full of advertisements for now forgotten brands.
examples.cn: 旧报纸上满是如今已被遗忘的品牌广告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德歪台斯门」——门上一贴，路人便看见：一则广告

root: 由 advertise 加名词后缀 -ment 构成；advertise 出自拉丁语 advertere「转向、使注意」（ad-「向」+ vertere「转」）。十七世纪时 advertisement 原指「通告、消息」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of advertisement keep one object, a turned notice: a paid sales pitch, a public announcement, a vacancy notice, and a living body that recommends by being seen.
sensesIntro.cn: advertisement 的四个义项都保留同一个物件——被转过来的告示：付费的推销、公开的通告、招聘告示，以及靠被人看见来推荐的活人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small boxed square inside a page reaches out and stops the hand that was turning it.
core.cn: 核心意象：版面上一个被框起来的小方块伸出手，拦住正要翻页的那只手。

branches.en: THE MARKET: the notice is paid for by a seller and asks for money.
branches.cn: 市场线：告示由卖方付费，最终是要人掏钱。

branches.en: THE BOARD: no one is selling anything, the notice only informs.
branches.cn: 告示板线：没有人在卖东西，告示只负责告知。

branches.en: THE VACANCY: the notice faces applicants rather than buyers.
branches.cn: 空缺线：告示朝向申请者而不是买家。

branches.en: THE BODY: the sign becomes a person who recommends by being seen.
branches.cn: 身体线：招牌变成一个人，靠被人看见来完成推荐。

branches.en: THE OLD WORD: selling and informing still share one noun, which is why a notice can be an ad.
branches.cn: 旧词线：销售与告知共用一个名词，所以一则通知也可以叫 ad。

intro.en: Advertisement is an English noun built on a Latin verb of turning; the suffix -ment is the only purely English piece.
intro.cn: advertisement 是建立在拉丁语「转」动词之上的英语名词，后缀 -ment 是其中唯一纯粹的英语成分。

latinIntro.en: Vertere and advertere are recorded Latin verbs, and advertir is recorded Old French, so the core needs no reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: vertere 与 advertere 是有文献的拉丁语动词，advertir 也是有文献的古法语，核心部分无需重构。

items.example: It gives the turning a target.
The verb supplies the physical gesture.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供那个物理动作。

items.example: It is the ancestor of advertise.
The noun is built on this verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词建立在它的动词之上。

items.meaning: a public notice or commercial ad

items.example: It is shorter than the full noun.
items.exampleCN: 它比完整的那个名词更短。

items.example: It turns a verb into a thing.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成一个「东西」。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -ment 回到动词形式，义为「做广告；宣传」
由同族动词 advertise 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「广告主；登广告的人」
由同族动词 advertise 加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告活动」
由本词截短而来，义为「广告」，是英式口语里的简短说法

definition_zh: 建议；意见；忠告；专业意见；（商业）通知
definition_en: an opinion or suggestion offered to someone about what they should do or how to act
core_image: 有人在耳边轻声指了一下前面的岔路口
scene: 年轻人站在岔路口，迟迟不肯迈步，身旁的长辈只说了一句话。A single piece of advice changed his mind at the crossroads.
sceneCN: 这里 advice 是「建议」（第 1 个义项：就该怎么做事提出的看法）；句意为一条建议让他在岔路口改变了主意。

pos.zh: 名词：建议；意见；忠告；专业意见；商业通知（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 由同一词源的古法语动词进入英语，义为「建议；劝告；通知」
由同族动词 advise 加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「明智的；可取的」
由同族动词 advise 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「顾问；提供意见的人」
由同族动词 advise 加形容词后缀 -ory 构成，义为「咨询的；劝告性的」

senses.title: A suggestion about what to do
senses.definition: an opinion given to help someone decide how to act, without any force behind it
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助某人决定如何行动而提出的看法，不具有强制力
senses.example: Her advice was to wait a week before signing the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 她的建议是先等一周再签合同。
senses.why: Old French avis meant an opinion, literally what seems to me; advice is that opinion handed to someone else.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 avis 意为「看法」，字面是「在我看来」；advice 就是被递给别人的那份看法。

senses.title: Earnest counsel about a danger
senses.definition: serious advice urging someone to avoid a course of action that is likely to harm them
senses.definitionCN: 郑重劝人避开可能带来伤害的做法，带有告诫意味
senses.example: He ignored his father's advice and drove through the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 他无视父亲的忠告，冒雨开车出发了。
senses.why: The same opinion becomes warmer and more urgent when danger is near, so the word can mean a warning offered out of care.
senses.whyCN: 危险临近时，同一份看法会变得更热切、更急迫，因此这个词也能指出于关心而给的告诫。

senses.title: Professional opinion
senses.definition: the considered opinion of a lawyer, doctor or other expert, usually paid for
senses.definitionCN: 律师、医生或其他专家经过斟酌的意见，通常付费获得
senses.example: The tenants paid for legal advice before moving out.
senses.exampleCN: 租户在搬走之前花钱获取了法律意见。
senses.why: An opinion from someone who knows the field carries more weight, so advice shifts from a favour to a service.
senses.whyCN: 来自内行的看法分量更重，advice 于是从「人情」变成一项「服务」。

senses.title: A formal business notification
senses.definition: a formal notice sent by a bank, shipper or office to inform a client of a transaction or shipment
senses.definitionCN: 银行、船运方或办公室发出的正式通知，向客户说明某笔交易或货运情况
senses.example: The bank sent an advice of the transfer to both parties.
senses.exampleCN: 银行向双方都发送了这笔转账的通知单。
senses.why: Commerce kept the older sense of informing rather than counselling: an advice note simply tells you what has happened.
senses.whyCN: 商业保留了较早的「告知」而非「劝告」义：advice note 只是告诉你已经发生了什么。

intro.en: Advice goes back to Old French avis, an opinion; how that word itself arose is explained in more than one way.
intro.cn: advice 可上溯至古法语 avis「看法」；至于 avis 本身如何产生，则有不止一种解释。

items.en: The usual account derives avis from the phrase ce m'est a vis, it seems to me; a link with Latin ad visum, according to what is seen, has also been suggested, and the sources do not agree.
items.cn: 通常的说法认为 avis 出自短语 ce m'est a vis「在我看来」；也有人提出它与拉丁语 ad visum「依所见」有关，各家解释并不一致。

items.en: Avis meant opinion, judgement, view; the word was used for what a person thought ought to be done.
items.cn: avis 意为「看法、判断、观点」，用来指一个人认为该怎么做。

items.en: The form avis or avice passed into English through Anglo-Norman, where spellings varied.
items.cn: avis 或 avice 这种形式经由盎格鲁—诺曼法语进入英语，当时拼写并不统一。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the fourteenth century with both the opinion and the notice senses. Exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词自十四世纪起见于英语记录，「看法」与「通知」两义并存；确切年代不确定。

items.en: The uncountable use settled in, and commerce kept the informing sense in set phrases such as advice note.
items.cn: 不可数用法逐渐固定，商业则在 advice note 等固定短语里保留了「告知」义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the avis family with its c and s spellings; the near-meaning group gathers other forms of guidance.
note.cn: 形近组收 avis 词族及其 c 与 s 两种拼写；近义组收其他形式的各种指引。

entries.definition: The verb of the same origin: the noun keeps c, the verb takes s.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，与本词同源：名词保留 c，动词写作 s。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning sensible or worth doing, formed from advise plus -able.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明智的、可取的」，由 advise 加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to give advice; also spelled advisor.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「顾问」，指以提建议为职责的人，也可拼作 advisor。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning giving advice rather than making decisions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「咨询的、劝告性的」，指只提意见而不作决定。

entries.definition: An idea offered for consideration; lighter and less personal than advice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「提议、建议」，比 advice 更轻、更不带个人色彩。

entries.definition: Serious advice, often legal; formal and weightier than advice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「忠告；法律意见」，语气正式，分量比 advice 更重。

entries.definition: Help in deciding a course of action, often over a longer period.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指导、指引」，常指较长时间内的方向性帮助。

entries.definition: A statement about danger; advice can warn, but a warning only warns.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「警告」，advice 可以包含警告，而 warning 只负责警告。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real avis root and the phrases advice actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 avis 词根，以及 advice 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Advice and advise differ by one letter: the noun keeps c, the verb takes s.
normal.cn: advice 与 advise 只差一个字母：名词保留 c，动词写作 s。

normal.en: Old French avis meant opinion, and it is the source of both forms.
normal.cn: 古法语 avis 意为「看法」，是两种形式的共同来源。

normal.en: A piece of advice is counted in pieces, because the noun is uncountable.
normal.cn: 一条建议用 a piece of advice 来计数，因为这个词不可数。

normal.en: Legal advice is an expert opinion you pay a professional for.
normal.cn: legal advice 是你付钱给专业人士换来的内行意见。

normal.en: An advice note in trade is a letter that informs, not a suggestion.
normal.cn: 商业里的 advice note 是一封告知函，而不是一条建议。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing at a fork in the road: it shows the way but does not push you along it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在岔路口指了指：它指出方向，却不推着你走。

abstract.en: The same hand can be a father's warning, a lawyer's note or a bank's statement; only the voice changes.
abstract.cn: 同一只手可以是父亲的告诫、律师的便笺或银行的说明，变的只是说话的声音。

abstract.en: Advice is always countable in weight but not in grammar, so it comes in pieces.
abstract.cn: 建议在分量上可以数，在语法上却不可数，因此只能一条一条地说。

examples.en: He asked for advice and then did the opposite.
examples.cn: 他征求了建议，然后做了相反的事。

examples.en: Good advice is easier to give than to follow.
examples.cn: 好建议给起来容易，做起来难。

examples.en: The lawyer's advice saved them a long and costly case.
examples.cn: 律师的建议让他们免去了一场漫长而昂贵的官司。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿外斯」——阿外小声在耳边说一句，路就选对了：建议

root: 古法语 avis「意见、看法」一般被认为出自短语 ce m'est a vis「在我看来」，也有人主张与拉丁语 ad visum「依所见」有关；具体来源有不同解释，属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of advice all deliver one thing, an opinion placed beside someone: a suggestion, a warning, an expert view, and a business notice that informs.
sensesIntro.cn: advice 的四个义项都在递出同一样东西——放在某人身边的一份看法：建议、告诫、专家意见，以及只负责告知的商业通知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand points at a fork in the road, showing the way without pushing anyone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在岔路口指了方向，只指路，不推人。

branches.en: THE OPINION: what seems to me is handed over as a proposal.
branches.cn: 看法线：「在我看来」的东西被递出去，成为一条提议。

branches.en: THE WARNING: when danger is near, the same opinion becomes urgent.
branches.cn: 告诫线：危险临近时，同一份看法变得急迫。

branches.en: THE EXPERT: knowledge makes the opinion a paid service.
branches.cn: 专家线：知识让这份看法变成付费服务。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: trade keeps only the informing half of the word.
branches.cn: 账册线：商业只保留了这个词「告知」的那一半。

branches.en: THE VOICE: suggestion and warning are the same words spoken louder.
branches.cn: 声音线：建议与告诫是同一句话，只是说得更响。

intro.en: Advice is a French noun of opinion; its family grew in English through the verb advise and a set of suffixes.
intro.cn: advice 是一个来自法语、表示「看法」的名词；它的词族在英语里靠动词 advise 与一组后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestry of avis is disputed, so only videre, to see, and visum, what is seen, are given here as recorded forms.
latinIntro.cn: avis 的拉丁语来源有争议，因此这里只列有文献的 videre「看见」与 visum「所见之物」。

items.example: It appears in the disputed Latin phrase behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在这个词背后那则有争议的拉丁短语里。

items.example: Seeing is one proposed source of the idea of opinion.
items.exampleCN: 「看见」是「看法」这一观念的一种可能来源。

items.structure: Latin participle used as a noun
items.example: The phrase ad visum means according to what is seen.
items.exampleCN: 短语 ad visum 意为「依所见」。

items.example: It is the direct ancestor of advice.
items.exampleCN: 它是 advice 的直接祖先。

items.example: The noun is uncountable in ordinary use.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词在日常用法中不可数。

items.example: The verb took the s spelling.
items.exampleCN: 动词采用了 s 的拼写。

definition_zh: 建议；劝告；通知；提供咨询
definition_en: to tell someone what you think they should do, or to inform someone formally about something
core_image: 一只手轻轻按住对方的胳膊，指向前方那条更稳的路
scene: 朋友准备在雨夜开车回家，另一个人拉住他的车门。I advised him to wait until the storm had passed.
sceneCN: 这里 advise 是「建议」（第 1 个义项：告诉某人应该怎么做）；句意为建议他等暴风雨过去再走。

pos.zh: 及物动词：建议；劝告；通知
不及物动词：提供意见；担任顾问

derivatives.zh: 由同一词源的法语名词进入英语，义为「建议；忠告；通知」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「顾问；提供意见的人」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ory 构成，义为「咨询的；劝告性的」

senses.title: To recommend a course of action
senses.definition: to tell someone what you think they should do, leaving the decision to them
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人你认为他应该怎么做，但把决定权留给他
senses.example: The doctor advised him to rest for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议他休息一周。
senses.why: Old French aviser meant to consider and then form a view, so the verb is the act of handing that view to someone else.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 aviser 意为先思量、再形成看法，因此这个动词就是把那份看法递到别人手里的动作。

senses.title: To urge against something
senses.definition: to warn someone strongly not to do something because it is dangerous or unwise
senses.definitionCN: 强烈告诫某人不要做某事，因为那很危险或不明智
senses.example: The coastguard advised against sailing in the gale.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸警卫队劝告人们不要在大风中出海。
senses.why: The same opinion can be spoken in the opposite direction: instead of pointing at the safer road, it pushes the person away from the cliff.
senses.whyCN: 同一份看法也可以朝反方向说：它不指向更稳的路，而是把人从悬崖边推开。

senses.title: To inform someone formally
senses.definition: to give someone official information, especially in business or legal writing
senses.definitionCN: 向某人提供正式信息，尤见于商业或法律文书
senses.example: Please be advised that the office will close at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 特此通知，办公室将在中午闭馆。
senses.why: The old sense of aviser was simply to give notice; in formal writing the verb still means to tell, with no suggestion attached.
senses.whyCN: aviser 的旧义就是「发出通知」；在正式文书里，这个动词仍只表示告知，不附带建议。

senses.title: To give expert guidance
senses.definition: to act as a consultant, giving regular professional opinions on a subject
senses.definitionCN: 担任顾问，就某一领域定期提供专业意见
senses.example: She advises the ministry on energy policy.
senses.exampleCN: 她就能源政策向该部提供咨询。
senses.why: When the advice is repeated and paid for, the verb stops being one favour and becomes a standing role.
senses.whyCN: 当建议反复给出并带有报酬时，这个动词就不再是一次人情，而成为一种长期角色。

intro.en: Advise is the verb twin of advice, coming from Old French aviser; the two words split only in spelling.
intro.cn: advise 是 advice 的动词孪生形式，来自古法语 aviser；两个词只在拼写上分了家。

items.en: Videre meant to see; one explanation of avis connects the idea of opinion with what is seen.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」；关于 avis 的一种解释，把「看法」与「所见」联系起来。

items.en: Some accounts link the word to ad visum, according to what is seen; others derive it from ce m'est a vis, and the question remains open.
items.cn: 有些说法把这个词与 ad visum「依所见」联系起来；另一些则认为出自 ce m'est a vis，这个问题仍无定论。

items.en: Aviser meant to consider, to form an opinion, and then to tell someone that opinion.
items.cn: aviser 意为「思量、形成看法」，随后把这个看法告诉别人。

items.en: English adopted the verb with forms such as avisen and advisen; the modern spelling settled later.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词时写作 avisen、advisen 等形式，现代拼写后来才固定。

items.en: The formal notice use survives in business letters, while everyday use settled on giving opinions about action.
items.cn: 正式的「通知」用法残留在商业信函里，日常用法则固定在「就行动给出意见」上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the c and s spellings of one family; the near-meaning group separates recommending, warning and informing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族里 c 与 s 两种拼写；近义组区分建议、警告与告知三类动作。

entries.definition: The uncountable noun of the same origin; it keeps c where the verb keeps s.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「建议」，与本词同源且不可数；名词写 c，动词写 s。

entries.definition: One who advises regularly, often in an official role.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「顾问」，指定期提供意见、常带官方身份的人。

entries.definition: An adjective for a body or note that gives advice without power to decide.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「咨询的、劝告性的」，指只提意见而无决定权的机构或文件。

entries.definition: Worth doing or sensible; formed with -able from the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明智的、可取的」，由动词加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: To suggest something as good or worth choosing; warmer and more positive.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推荐」，语气更积极，强调某物值得选择。

entries.definition: To give serious or professional advice, especially in law or therapy.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「劝告、提供专业辅导」，多用于法律或心理领域，语气正式。

entries.definition: To tell someone about a danger; it covers only the advise against sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「警告」，只对应本词第 2 个义项。

entries.definition: To give someone facts; it covers the formal notice sense without any opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「通知、告知」，对应本词第 3 个义项，但不含任何意见。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real aviser root and the phrases advise actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 aviser 词根，以及 advise 实际构成的搭配。

normal.en: The verb ends in the s sound and is written with s; the noun keeps c.
normal.cn: 动词读作 z 音、写作 s；名词则保留 c。

normal.en: Aviser in Old French meant to consider and then give an opinion.
normal.cn: 古法语 aviser 意为先思量、再给出看法。

normal.en: Advise against is the warning branch: the hand pushes the other way.
normal.cn: advise against 是警告的那条分支：手把人往反方向推。

normal.en: Please be advised that is a formal notice, not a suggestion.
normal.cn: please be advised that 是正式通知，不是建议。

normal.en: An adviser is the person who does the advising.
normal.cn: adviser 就是那个「提建议」的人。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on someone's sleeve, pointing at the safer road but leaving the choice open.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手搭在别人的袖子上，指向更稳的那条路，却把选择留给对方。

abstract.en: The same hand can turn the person away from a cliff, or hand over a printed notice instead.
abstract.cn: 同一只手也可以把人从悬崖边拉回，或者干脆递过去一张印好的通知。

abstract.en: Give the hand a salary and it becomes an adviser, sitting at the table every week.
abstract.cn: 给这只手一份薪水，它就变成顾问，每周坐在桌边。

examples.en: Teachers advise students to read the question twice.
examples.cn: 老师建议学生把题目读两遍。

examples.en: He advised us against buying the flat without a survey.
examples.cn: 他劝我们不要在没做勘察的情况下买下那套公寓。

examples.en: She advises several small firms on tax matters.
examples.cn: 她为几家小公司提供税务方面的咨询。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿外兹」——阿外指着那条稳路，劝你别走险道：劝告

root: 古法语 aviser 与 advice 同源，一般追溯到 avis「看法」，可能与拉丁语 ad visum「依所见」相关，也可能出自短语 ce m'est a vis「在我看来」；确切来源有不同解释。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of advise all hand over one opinion: a recommendation, a warning, a formal piece of information, and a standing professional role.
sensesIntro.cn: advise 的四个义项都在递出同一份看法：一条建议、一句告诫、一则正式信息，以及一个长期的顾问身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand rests on someone's sleeve and points at the steadier road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在别人的袖子上，指向更稳的那条路。

branches.en: THE PROPOSAL: an opinion is formed and handed over for the other to use.
branches.cn: 提议线：看法先被形成，再递出去供对方使用。

branches.en: THE BRAKE: the same opinion is spoken as a push away from danger.
branches.cn: 刹车线：同一份看法以「把人推离危险」的方式说出来。

branches.en: THE NOTICE: only the telling remains, with no view attached.
branches.cn: 通知线：只剩下「告知」，不附带任何看法。

branches.en: THE CHAIR: repeated giving turns the act into a post at the table.
branches.cn: 席位线：反复给出意见，使这个动作变成桌边的一个职位。

branches.en: THE SAME MOUTH: a consultant and a friend give the same kind of sentence, only the contract differs.
branches.cn: 同一张嘴：顾问与朋友说的是同一类句子，不同的只是有没有合约。

intro.en: Advise is the verb half of a French pair; English added the person, the adjective and the abstract forms.
intro.cn: advise 是一对法语词中的动词那一半；英语又补出表示人、形容词与抽象概念的派生形式。

latinIntro.en: Videre and visum are recorded Latin words, but the link between avis and them is disputed, so it is described as uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: videre 与 visum 是有文献的拉丁语词，但 avis 与它们的关系存在争议，因此只按「不确定」来表述。

items.example: It appears in the disputed Latin phrase behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在这个词背后那则有争议的拉丁短语里。

items.example: Seeing is one proposed source of the notion of opinion.
items.exampleCN: 「看见」是「看法」这一观念的一种可能来源。

items.example: The phrase ad visum means according to what is seen.
items.exampleCN: 短语 ad visum 意为「依所见」。

items.example: The verb carries all three everyday senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词承担了三个日常义项。

definition_en: to speak or argue in public support of a cause or a person, or a person who does this, especially a lawyer who pleads a case
core_image: 法庭上一个人站到当事人前面，替他开口说话
scene: 听证会开始前，一位医生站在居民们前面，替他们陈述理由。A local doctor advocated cleaner air at the public hearing.
sceneCN: 这里 advocate 是「提倡、主张」（第 1 个义项：公开支持某项主张）；句意为一位本地医生在听证会上主张更清洁的空气。

pos.zh: 及物动词：提倡；主张；为……辩护
不及物动词：主张；为……发声
名词：拥护者；提倡者；辩护律师

由本词加表示人的后缀 -or 构成，义为「拥护者；提倡者」

senses.title: To support a cause publicly
senses.definition: to speak or write in public support of a policy, idea or way of doing things
senses.definitionCN: 公开以言语或文字支持某项政策、理念或做法
senses.example: Several doctors advocated a ban on smoking in restaurants.
senses.exampleCN: 几位医生主张在餐厅内禁烟。
senses.why: Latin advocare meant to call someone to one's aid, so advocating is calling other people to stand behind a cause.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 advocare 意为「召人来相助」，因此 advocate 就是召来众人站到某项主张背后。

senses.title: To speak in defence of a person
senses.definition: to argue on behalf of a person or group who is being criticised or attacked
senses.definitionCN: 为受到批评或攻击的个人或群体申辩
senses.example: The union advocated the dismissed workers at the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 工会在听证会上为被解雇的工人辩护。
senses.why: The person called to help stands in front of the accused: the same root, but now the body being shielded is a human being.
senses.whyCN: 被召来相助的人站到被指责者的前面：词根不变，只是被挡住的对象变成了一个活人。

senses.title: A supporter of a cause
senses.definition: a person who publicly supports a policy, idea or group over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期公开支持某项政策、理念或群体的个人
senses.example: She became an advocate of free public transport.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了一名主张免费公共交通的拥护者。
senses.why: The verb turns into the person who habitually performs it: the one who keeps calling others to the cause.
senses.whyCN: 动词转指习惯性做这件事的人：那个不断号召他人加入主张的人。

senses.title: A lawyer who pleads in court
senses.definition: a lawyer, especially in Scottish or church courts, who presents a case and speaks for a client
senses.definitionCN: 尤指苏格兰或教会法庭上代表当事人陈述案件的律师
senses.example: The advocate rose to question the witness.
senses.exampleCN: 辩护律师起身向证人提问。
senses.why: Roman advocates were friends called in to plead for a client; the modern courtroom kept the name for the person who speaks in another's place.
senses.whyCN: 古罗马的 advocatus 是被召来替当事人陈情的友人；现代法庭保留了这个称呼，指替别人开口的人。

intro.en: Advocate is Latin for one called to help, built on the verb for calling; English took it almost unchanged.
intro.cn: advocate 在拉丁语里指「被召来相助的人」，建立在表示「呼叫」的动词上；英语几乎原样借入。

items.en: Vocare meant to call, and it also gave vocal, voice and vocation.
items.cn: vocare 意为「呼叫」，还生出 vocal、voice 与 vocation。

items.en: Ad plus vocare gave advocare, to call someone to one's aid, especially in a legal dispute.
items.cn: ad- 与 vocare 合成 advocare，意为「召人来相助」，尤用于法律纠纷。

items.en: Advocatus was the person so called: a friend or adviser who stood beside a litigant and pleaded for him.
items.cn: advocatus 就是被召来的那个人：站在诉讼人身边替他陈情的朋友或顾问。

items.en: English took advocate directly from Latin; the legal sense came first and the general verb sense followed much later.
items.cn: 英语直接从拉丁语借入 advocate；法律义先出现，一般性的动词义要晚得多。

items.en: Scottish courts kept advocate for a barrister, while everyday English made the verb mean public support of any cause.
items.cn: 苏格兰法庭保留 advocate 指出庭律师；日常英语则把这个动词用作对任何主张的公开支持。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the calling family; the near-meaning group gathers people who back a cause and one who opposes them.
note.cn: 形近组收「呼叫」词族；近义组收支持某项主张的人，以及站在对面的人。

entries.definition: The noun for the activity of publicly supporting a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「倡导、拥护」，指公开支持某项主张的活动。

entries.definition: A rarer word for a person who advocates something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「拥护者」，是较少见的同义说法。

entries.definition: The grammatical case used when addressing someone; the same calling root, a different branch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「呼格」，即称呼人时使用的语法格；与本词同出 vocare，但走的是另一条分支。

entries.definition: A person who argues in favour of a proposal or theory.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支持者、主张者」，指为某项提议或理论辩护的人。

entries.definition: A general word for someone who backs a person, team or idea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支持者」，泛指站在某人、某队或某理念一边的人。

entries.definition: To champion is to fight actively for a cause, stronger and more public than advocate.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「积极捍卫、为……奔走」，比 advocate 更强调主动与公开。

entries.definition: A person who argues against a cause, the natural opposite of an advocate.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「反对者」，是拥护者的天然对立面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin calling verb and the phrases advocate actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「呼叫」动词，以及 advocate 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Advocatus is one called to help: ad plus vocare, to call.
normal.cn: advocatus 是「被召来相助的人」：ad 加 vocare「呼叫」。

normal.en: Advocate, advocacy and advocator all keep the calling root.
normal.cn: advocate、advocacy 与 advocator 都保留了「呼叫」这个词根。

normal.en: In Scotland an advocate is what England calls a barrister.
normal.cn: 在苏格兰，advocate 就是英格兰所说的 barrister（出庭律师）。

normal.en: To advocate for something is to call others to its side.
normal.cn: advocate for 某物，就是把别人召到它这一边。

normal.en: The devil's advocate argues the other side on purpose, for the sake of the argument.
normal.cn: devil's advocate 是为了把讨论推深而故意站到对面的人。

abstract.en: Picture a person stepping in front of someone accused and speaking in that person's place.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走到被指责者的前面，替那个人开口。

abstract.en: The same figure can stand before a whole cause instead of one person: a policy, a river, a school.
abstract.cn: 同一个人也可以站在一整项主张前面，而不是某个人前面：一项政策、一条河、一所学校。

abstract.en: The voice is the only tool: nothing is built, only called for until others join.
abstract.cn: 唯一的工具是声音：什么也没造出来，只是一直呼叫，直到别人加入。

examples.en: Many teachers advocate more time for play in primary school.
examples.cn: 许多教师主张在小学阶段多留一些玩耍的时间。

examples.en: He advocated for the tenants when the landlord raised the rent.
examples.cn: 房东涨租时，他为租户们发声。

examples.en: The advocate for the family asked for a shorter hearing.
examples.cn: 这家人的辩护律师请求缩短听证时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃凯特」——阿德站到当事人前面，替他开口：拥护

root: 拉丁语 advocatus「被召来相助的人」来自 advocare「召来」，由 ad-「向」+ vocare「呼叫」构成；古罗马的 advocatus 是陪当事人出庭的友人，后来专指辩护律师。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of advocate all stage one scene, a person standing in front and speaking for another: a cause, an accused person, a lifelong supporter, and a lawyer in court.
sensesIntro.cn: advocate 的四个义项都在上演同一幕——一个人站到前面替别人说话：为一项主张、为一个被指责的人、为一个长期的支持者身份，以及为法庭上的当事人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure steps in front of the accused and speaks in that person's place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人走到被指责者的前面，替那个人开口。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: the voice is raised for a policy rather than for a person.
branches.cn: 主张线：被抬高的是为某项政策而非为某个人发声。

branches.en: THE ACCUSED: the body in front shields a person who is under attack.
branches.cn: 受责线：站在前面的身体挡住的是一个正被攻击的人。

branches.en: THE ROLE: repeating the act turns it into an identity people recognise.
branches.cn: 身份线：反复做这个动作，使它变成一种被人认出的身份。

branches.en: THE COURT: the old Roman helper becomes a licensed speaker in court.
branches.cn: 法庭线：古罗马的相助者变成了法庭上有资格的发言人。

branches.en: THE SAME STANDING PLACE: defending a worker and defending a client use one position.
branches.cn: 同一个站位：为工人辩护与为当事人辩护用的是同一个位置。

intro.en: Advocate is a Latin prefix plus the Latin verb for calling; English added only a few suffixes.
intro.cn: advocate 是一个拉丁语前缀加表示「呼叫」的拉丁动词；英语只补了少量后缀。

latinIntro.en: Vocare, advocare and advocatus are all attested Latin forms, so the core needs no reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: vocare、advocare 与 advocatus 都是有文献的拉丁语形式，核心部分无需重构。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词还生出 vocal 与 voice。
