definition_zh: 飞机；航空器（宽松用法）；英式拼写形式（对应美式 airplane）
definition_en: a powered aircraft with fixed wings that is heavier than air and flies by the lift produced by its wings
core_image: 一对固定的翅膀切开空气，把沉重的机身托起来
scene: 雨后的机场跑道上，一架银色的机器正缓缓抬头。The aeroplane lifted its nose and climbed into the grey sky.
sceneCN: 这里 aeroplane 是「固定翼动力飞机」（第 1 个义项：有发动机和固定机翼的航空器）；句意为那架飞机抬起机头，爬升进入灰色的天空。

pos.zh: 名词：飞机；航空器；英式拼写形式

derivatives.zh: 由 air 与 plane 拼合而成的美式对应形式，义为「飞机」，与英式 aeroplane 指同一物
由 plane 加前缀 sea- 构成的复合词，义为「水上飞机」

senses.title: A powered fixed-wing aircraft
senses.definition: an aircraft driven by an engine, with fixed wings, that is heavier than air and flies by the lift of those wings
senses.definitionCN: 由发动机驱动、带固定机翼、重于空气并依靠机翼升力飞行的航空器
senses.example: The aeroplane climbed steeply after take-off.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机起飞后急剧爬升。
senses.why: The word joins Greek air to Latin flat: the flat surfaces are what hold the heavy machine up, so the name describes the wing before it describes the flight.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把希腊语的「空气」与拉丁语的「平坦」接在一起：托起沉重机身的正是那些平坦的面，所以这个名字先说机翼，再说飞行。

senses.title: Any flying craft, loosely
senses.definition: used loosely, especially in older writing, for any machine that flies, including craft without fixed wings
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在较早的文本中宽松地指任何能飞的机器，包括没有固定机翼的飞行器
senses.example: Old posters showed an aeroplane with flapping wings, though no such craft ever flew.
senses.exampleCN: 旧海报上画着一架拍动翅膀的飞机，尽管这样的飞行器从未真正飞起来。
senses.why: Before the fixed-wing machine existed, the word covered whatever people imagined could fly, so the loose use is older than the strict one.
senses.whyCN: 在固定翼飞机出现之前，这个词覆盖人们想象中一切能飞的东西，因此宽松用法比严格用法更早。

senses.title: The British spelling of airplane
senses.titleCN: 英式拼写形式（与美式 airplane 对应）
senses.definition: the spelling used in British English for the aircraft that American English usually calls airplane
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语使用的拼写，与美式英语通常写作 airplane 的同一飞行器对应
senses.example: British newspapers write aeroplane where American ones write airplane.
senses.exampleCN: 英国报纸写作 aeroplane，而美国报纸写作 airplane。
senses.why: This is a difference of spelling and register rather than of meaning: one word, two written shapes, each tied to a national variety.
senses.whyCN: 这是拼写与语域的差别，而不是意义的差别：同一个词有两种书写形状，各自绑定一种国别变体。

intro.en: Aeroplane is a French coinage that mixes a Greek word for air with a Latin word for flat, then passes into English.
intro.cn: aeroplane 是法语造出的词，把希腊语表示「空气」的词与拉丁语表示「平坦」的词混合起来，随后进入英语。

items.en: Greek aēr meant air, the lower atmosphere; it is the source of the aero- element in many technical words.
items.cn: 希腊语 aēr 意为「空气」，指下层大气；它是许多技术词里 aero- 这一成分的来源。

items.en: Latin planus meant flat, level, and gave the plane of a surface as well as the plane of a wing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 planus 意为「平坦的、水平的」，既生出「平面」，也生出「机翼面」。

items.en: French coined aéroplane in the 1850s from these two pieces, first for a flying machine or a wing surface. The exact coinage date is uncertain.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪五十年代用这两个成分造出 aéroplane，最早指飞行机器或机翼面；确切造词年代不确定。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the later nineteenth century; after the first powered flights the fixed-wing sense became the standard one.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪后期借入这个词；在最初的动力飞行之后，固定翼飞机的含义成为标准义。

items.en: British English kept aeroplane, while American English reshaped it as airplane; both names still refer to the same machine.
items.cn: 英式英语保留 aeroplane，美式英语则改造成 airplane；两个名称指的仍是同一种机器。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the aero- and plane elements with their relatives; the near-meaning group gathers other flying craft.
note.cn: 形近组收 aero- 与 plane 两个成分及其亲属词；近义组收其他飞行器。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the same word, with air- in place of the Greek aero-.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「飞机」，是同一个词的美式拼写，用 air- 替换了希腊语的 aero-。

entries.definition: The science or practice of flying aircraft; it shares aero- but not the plane element.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航空学」，只共享 aero- 这一成分，不含 plane 部分。

entries.definition: An older British word for an airfield, built with aero- and a different second element.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机场」，是较旧的英式说法，由 aero- 与另一个成分构成。

entries.definition: Any machine that flies, including helicopters and gliders; wider than aeroplane.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航空器」，包括直升机与滑翔机，范围比 aeroplane 更宽。

entries.definition: A fast aircraft driven by jet engines; a type of aeroplane rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喷气式飞机」，是飞机的一种，而不是同义词。

entries.definition: A winged craft with no engine, so it does not fit the powered sense of aeroplane.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「滑翔机」，没有发动机，因此不符合飞机「有动力」这一层意思。

entries.definition: A craft lifted by rotating blades rather than by fixed wings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「直升机」，靠旋转桨叶而不是固定机翼获得升力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real building blocks of the word and the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个词真实的两个构件，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Aero- is Greek aēr, air; plane comes from Latin planus, flat.
normal.cn: aero- 是希腊语 aēr「空气」；plane 来自拉丁语 planus「平坦」。

normal.en: French coined aéroplane in the 1850s by joining these two pieces.
normal.cn: 法语在十九世纪五十年代把这两个构件拼成了 aéroplane。

normal.en: English kept aeroplane, while American English settled on airplane.
normal.cn: 英式英语保留 aeroplane，美式英语则定下 airplane。

normal.en: Aerodrome and aeronautics share the aero- element, not the whole word.
normal.cn: aerodrome 与 aeronautics 共享 aero- 这一成分，而不是整个词。

normal.en: A glider has wings too but no engine, so it is not an aeroplane in the strict sense.
normal.cn: 滑翔机也有机翼，但没有发动机，因此严格说来不算飞机。

abstract.en: Picture a flat board held out of a moving car: the air pushes up on it as it slips forward.
abstract.cn: 想象一块平板伸出行驶中的车窗：它向前滑时，空气把它往上托。

abstract.en: Give the board an engine and a tail, and it becomes the machine that lifts its nose on the runway.
abstract.cn: 给这块板装上发动机和尾巴，它就变成跑道上会抬起机头的那台机器。

abstract.en: The name itself is a mixed marriage: Greek air and a Latin flat surface, joined in French.
abstract.cn: 这个名字本身就是一场混合婚姻：希腊的空气与拉丁的平面，在法语里成亲。

examples.en: The aeroplane landed ten minutes late because of fog.
examples.cn: 由于大雾，飞机晚了十分钟降落。

examples.en: Model aeroplanes hung from the ceiling of the shop.
examples.cn: 商店的天花板上挂着几架模型飞机。

examples.en: On old maps the aeroplane appears as a strange winged shape.
examples.cn: 在旧地图上，飞机被画成一个奇怪的有翼形状。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱若普莱恩」——爱若把一块平板举到空中，它就飞起来了：飞机

root: 法语 aéroplane 由希腊语 aēr「空气」与拉丁语 planus「平坦的」拼合而成，属希腊—拉丁混合构词；最早指「飞行面」，二十世纪初固定翼飞机普及后专指飞机。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of aeroplane narrow from the strict machine, to the loose name for anything that flies, to the spelling that British English kept.
sensesIntro.cn: aeroplane 的三个义项由严到宽：严格的固定翼动力飞机、对一切飞行器的宽松称呼，以及英式英语保留的拼写形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of fixed wings cuts through the air and holds a heavy body up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一对固定的机翼切开空气，把沉重的机身托住。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: engine, fixed wing and lift are all required.
branches.cn: 机器线：发动机、固定机翼与升力三者缺一不可。

branches.en: THE LOOSE NAME: anything imagined to fly could once carry the word.
branches.cn: 宽泛命名线：过去凡是被想象能飞的东西都可以用这个词。

branches.en: THE SPELLING: British and American English split the written form, not the meaning.
branches.cn: 拼写线：英式与美式分开的是书写形式，而不是意义。

branches.en: THE SAME OBJECT: a newspaper on either side of the Atlantic names one machine.
branches.cn: 同一物体：大西洋两岸的报纸命名的是同一种机器。

branches.en: THE WORD ITSELF: the older name was broader, and the modern spelling is narrower in meaning.
branches.cn: 词自身：较早的名称含义更宽，而现代拼写对应的是更窄的机器。

intro.en: Aeroplane is built from a Greek prefix of air and a Latin root for flat; English added only the plural and some sibling compounds.
intro.cn: aeroplane 由希腊语表示「空气」的成分与拉丁语表示「平坦」的词根构成；英语只补了复数与一些同类复合词。

latinIntro.en: Planus and planum are recorded Latin words; aēr is Greek rather than Latin, which is why this is called a mixed compound.
latinIntro.cn: planus 与 planum 是有文献的拉丁语词；aēr 属希腊语而非拉丁语，因此这个词被称为混合构词。

items.example: It appears in aeroplane and aerodrome.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 aeroplane 与 aerodrome 里。

items.example: The Greek noun became the aero- prefix.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊语名词变成了 aero- 前缀。

items.example: The second element names the flat wing.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分命名的正是平坦的机翼。

items.exampleCN: 这个词先命名机翼，再命名飞行。

items.exampleCN: 它用 air- 替换了 aero-。

它同样以 aero- 开头。

definition_zh: 事情；事务；公共事务；私通；事件；社交活动
definition_en: a matter or set of events that has to be dealt with, ranging from a private task to public business and a romantic relationship
core_image: 手边一件待办的事，从私事一直铺到众人的大事
scene: 镇上的老茶馆里，两个人压低声音，说起昨天那桩闹得满城风雨的事。The whole affair was settled before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 affair 是「事件、事情」（第 4 个义项：作为整体来看的一桩事件）；句意为这整件事在中午之前就了结了。

pos.zh: 名词：事情；事务；公共事务；私通；事件；社交活动

derivatives.zh: 由本词加复数后缀 -s 构成，义为「事务；公共事务」，语义从单件「事情」偏移为「一批待办之事」
由 love 与 affair 复合，义为「恋情；风流韵事」，语义从泛指的「事」偏移为「私人之情」
借自法语的同形词，义为「丑闻；风流事件」，语义从「事情」偏移为「引人议论的私事」

senses.title: A matter to be dealt with
senses.definition: a thing that has to be done or dealt with, especially a practical or personal matter
senses.definitionCN: 需要去做或处理的事情，尤指实际事务或个人事务
senses.example: He had urgent affairs to settle before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前他还有急事要处理。
senses.why: Old French a faire literally meant 'to do', so an affair begins as something that has to be done.
senses.whyCN: 古法语短语 a faire 字面就是「去做」，所以 affair 最初指一件必须去做的事。

senses.title: Public or political business
senses.definition: the business of a government, organization or community, usually used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 政府、机构或共同体的事务，通常用复数形式
senses.example: She follows current affairs closely.
senses.exampleCN: 她密切关注时事。
senses.why: Many single tasks put together become one field of business, and the plural affairs names that field.
senses.whyCN: 许多单件的事情聚在一起就成了一片事务领域，复数 affairs 指的正是这片领域。

senses.title: A secret romantic relationship
senses.definition: a romantic or sexual relationship, especially one that is kept secret or is outside marriage
senses.definitionCN: 浪漫或两性的关系，尤指隐秘的或婚外的关系
senses.example: Their affair lasted less than a year.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的私情持续了不到一年。
senses.why: A private matter can be narrowed to its most private kind, and affair then carries the colour of a relationship kept out of sight.
senses.whyCN: 私事可以被缩到最私密的一种，于是 affair 带上了「不便公开的关系」这层色彩。

senses.title: An event or matter as a whole
senses.definition: an event, situation or series of events considered as a single whole, often with a judgment attached
senses.definitionCN: 被当作一个整体来看待的事件、情况或一连串事件，常附带评价
senses.example: The whole affair ended in an awkward silence.
senses.exampleCN: 整件事以一阵尴尬的沉默收场。
senses.why: Once the separate details are gathered under one name, the affair becomes the event seen as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把零散的细节收拢到同一个名称下，affair 就成了被整体看待的那桩事件。

senses.title: A social occasion
senses.definition: an organized social event or occasion, especially a formal or grand one
senses.definitionCN: 安排好的社交活动或场合，尤指正式、隆重的场合
senses.example: The garden party was a grand affair.
senses.exampleCN: 那场花园聚会办得十分隆重。
senses.why: A task can also be something arranged for people to attend, so the word moves from business to social occasion.
senses.whyCN: 待办之事也可以是为人安排、请人参加的活动，于是这个词从「事务」转向「社交场合」。

senses.title: A thing or article, now old-fashioned
senses.definition: a thing, object or article of a particular kind, an old-fashioned use that survives in a few phrases
senses.definitionCN: 某类东西、物件，属旧式用法，仅存于少数短语中
senses.example: She packed her affairs into a single trunk.
senses.exampleCN: 她把自己的物件都装进了一只箱子。
senses.why: The earliest sense covered anything one had to do with, and a few old phrases still use affairs for belongings.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项涵盖一个人要打交道的任何东西，少数旧短语仍用 affairs 指随身物件。

intro.en: Affair comes from a French phrase meaning 'to do', built on the Latin verb for doing or making.
intro.cn: affair 来自一句意为「去做」的法语短语，其核心是拉丁语中表示「做、造」的动词。

items.en: facere meant 'to do, make', and it is one of the most productive verbs in the Latin family.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，是拉丁语词族中最能产出的动词之一。

items.en: The phrase a faire meant 'to do' or 'that which is to be done'; the noun afaire grew out of it.
items.cn: 短语 a faire 意为「去做」或「要做的事」，名词 afaire 正由它生长出来。

items.en: Middle English borrowed afaire in the fourteenth century with the sense of business or a matter in hand.
items.cn: 中古英语在十四世纪借入 afaire，意为「事务」或「手头的事情」。

items.en: The sense widened from a task to an event, a social occasion and, later, a romantic relationship.
items.cn: 词义从「任务」扩展到「事件」「社交场合」，后来又发展出「恋情」。

items.en: The plural affairs specialised in public and political business, while the singular kept the private and event senses.
items.cn: 复数 affairs 专门承担公共与政治事务，单数则保留私事与事件的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and borrowings built on the same French word; the near-meaning group gathers broader words for matters and events.
note.cn: 形近组收同一法语词构成的形式与借词；近义组收表示事情、事件的更宽泛的词。

entries.definition: A borrowing from French used in English for a scandal or a celebrated romantic episode.
entries.definitionCN: 借自法语的词，在英语中指丑闻或引人注目的风流事件，与本词同出法语 afaire。

entries.definition: The plural of affair, used especially for business, public matters or personal belongings.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的复数形式，尤指事务、公共事务或随身物件。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to influence; it shares the fac- root but comes through afficere, so it only looks close.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「影响」；它共享 fac- 词根，但经由 afficere 而来，只是与本词形近。

entries.definition: A subject or situation being dealt with; the most neutral word for an affair in the sense of a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事情、问题」，是 affair「事情」义最中性的对应词。

entries.definition: Work, duties or concerns that one is responsible for; close to the public affairs sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事务、职责」，与 affair 的公共事务义接近。

entries.definition: Something that happens, especially something important; close to the whole-event sense of affair.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件」，尤指重要之事，与 affair 的「整件事」义接近。

entries.definition: A particular time or a special event; close to the social-occasion sense of affair.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「场合、时机」，与 affair 的「社交活动」义接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French phrase behind the word and the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词背后真实的法语短语，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: a faire means 'to do': an affair is first of all something to be done.
normal.cn: a faire 意为「去做」：affair 首先是某件要去做的事。

normal.en: The Latin verb facere 'to make' also gives fact, factory and effect.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词 facere「做、造」还生出 fact、factory 与 effect。

normal.en: Public affairs and current affairs keep the plural for the business of many people.
normal.cn: public affairs 与 current affairs 用复数表示许多人的共同事务。

normal.en: A love affair narrows the private matter to a relationship kept out of sight.
normal.cn: a love affair 把私事缩窄为一段不公开的关系。

normal.en: The whole affair treats every detail as one single event.
normal.cn: the whole affair 把所有细节当作同一桩事件。

abstract.en: Picture a single sheet on a desk with one line written on it: to do.
abstract.cn: 想象书桌上只有一张纸，上面写着一行字：要做。

abstract.en: The same sheet multiplies into a stack of files for a government, or folds into one sealed envelope for a secret romance.
abstract.cn: 同一张纸可以增殖成政府的一摞文件，也可以折成一封密封的信，装下一段隐秘恋情。

abstract.en: The word always keeps that notebook feel: something is on hand and waiting to be handled.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终保留着记事本的感觉：有件事摆在手边，等着被处理。

examples.en: She had no time for the routine affairs of the office.
examples.cn: 她没时间处理办公室的日常事务。

examples.en: The wedding was a quiet family affair.
examples.cn: 那场婚礼是一次安静的家庭聚会。

examples.en: He denied the affair with his colleague.
examples.cn: 他否认了与同事的私情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿费尔」——阿婆费心操办的一件件事：事情、事务

root: 古法语 afaire 来自短语 a faire「要做的事」，faire 又出自拉丁语 facere「做、造」。英语在十四世纪借入，由「待办之事」扩展出「公共事务、事件、恋情、社交活动」等义；更早的印欧来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of affair all start from one thing on hand: a task, the business of many, a hidden romance, an event seen whole, a social occasion, and an old word for belongings.
sensesIntro.cn: affair 的六个义项都从手边的一件事出发：一件任务、众人的事务、隐秘的恋情、被整体看待的事件、社交场合，以及指物件的旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sheet marked 'to do' lies on a desk, ready to be handled.
core.cn: 核心意象：书桌上放着一张写着「要做」的纸，等着被处理。

branches.en: THE TASK: an affair begins as something that has to be done.
branches.cn: 任务线：affair 最初就是一件必须去做的事。

branches.en: THE BUSINESS: many tasks gathered together become public affairs.
branches.cn: 事务线：许多任务汇在一起，就成了公共事务。

branches.en: THE SECRET: the private matter narrows into a relationship kept out of sight.
branches.cn: 私密线：私事收窄成一段不公开的关系。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: all the details are gathered and judged as one event.
branches.cn: 整体线：所有细节被收拢，当作一桩事件来评价。

branches.en: THE OCCASION: the task becomes a social gathering, and an older use still calls belongings affairs.
branches.cn: 场合线：事情变成社交聚会，更旧的用法仍用 affairs 指随身物件。

intro.en: Affair is a French phrase frozen into an English noun; its parts are a preposition and the verb 'to do'.
intro.cn: affair 是一句凝固成英语名词的法语短语，其成分是一个介词与表示「做」的动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb facere and its noun factum are recorded, so the Latin list can be filled with real forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 facere 及其名词 factum 均有文献记录，因此拉丁同族一栏可以填入真实词形。

Faire is the verb inside afaire.
items.exampleCN: faire 是 afaire 当中的动词。

items.example: Facere is the source of the French verb.
items.exampleCN: facere 是那个法语动词的来源。

items.example: It appears in fact and factor.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 fact 与 factor 中。

items.example: It fused the preposition with the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它把介词与动词黏合在一起。

items.example: The press called it a political affaire.
items.exampleCN: 媒体称之为一桩政治丑闻。

definition_zh: 影响；感动；假装；侵袭；偏爱（旧义）
definition_en: to produce a change in someone or something, to move someone emotionally, or to pretend to have a quality
core_image: 一只手伸到对象身上，把它的状态轻轻推偏
scene: 暴雨过后，村里通往镇上的土路多处塌方，进出都要绕很远。Heavy rain affected the road to the town for a week.
sceneCN: 这里 affect 是「影响」（第 1 个义项：对某物产生作用或改变）；句意为大雨使通往镇上的路受影响长达一周。

pos.zh: 动词：影响；感动；假装；侵袭

collocations.zh: 深受感动的；深受影响的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加过去分词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「做作的；受影响的」，语义从「被作用」偏移为「刻意装出的」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「感人至深的」，语义从「施加作用」偏移为「打动人心」
由拉丁词干加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「喜爱；感情」，语义从「被作用的状态」偏移为「被触动的情意」
由本词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「做作；装腔作势」，语义从「假装」偏移为「刻意不自然的表现」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词过去分词构成，义为「不满的；不再忠实的」，语义从「被影响」偏移为「被离心」

senses.title: To produce a change in something
senses.definition: to produce a change in a person, thing, situation or process
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某物、某种情况或过程产生改变
senses.example: The drought affected the harvest across the province.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱影响了全省的收成。
senses.why: Latin afficere meant to do something to a thing; the ad- points the action at the object, so affect is first a push that changes it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 afficere 意为「对某物做点什么」，前缀 ad- 把动作指向对象，所以 affect 最初就是一次改变对象的作用。

senses.title: To move someone emotionally
senses.definition: to touch or move someone's feelings, often strongly
senses.definitionCN: 触动或打动某人的情感，常指强烈触动
senses.example: The old soldier's story affected the whole audience.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老兵的故事打动了全场听众。
senses.why: If a thing can act on the body, it can also act on the feelings; the same push reaches the heart and leaves it changed.
senses.whyCN: 既然外物能作用于身体，它也能作用于情感；同一次推及抵达心里，让心被改变。

senses.title: To pretend to have a quality
senses.definition: to behave as if one has a feeling, manner or quality that one does not really have
senses.definitionCN: 表现得好像拥有某种并不真实的情感、举止或特质
senses.example: He affected an accent to amuse the children.
senses.exampleCN: 他装出一种口音来逗孩子们开心。
senses.why: The word can describe putting a state onto oneself, as if the action were performed on one's own surface; the result is a show.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能表示把某种状态「施加」到自己身上，仿佛动作做在自己的表层上，结果就是一场表演。

senses.title: To attack a part of the body
senses.definition: of a disease or condition, to attack or damage a part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病或某种状况侵袭、损害身体的某个部位
senses.example: The virus affected his lungs first.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒首先侵袭了他的肺部。
senses.why: A disease is an outside force acting on the body, and the part it reaches is the part it affects.
senses.whyCN: 疾病是一种作用于身体的外来力量，它抵达哪个部位，哪个部位就是被它侵袭的地方。

senses.title: To be fond of, in older usage
senses.definition: to like or be fond of something, an old-fashioned use now found mainly in older texts
senses.definitionCN: 喜欢、偏爱某物，属旧式用法，今多见于较早的文本
senses.example: The old earl affected country life above all things.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老伯爵格外偏爱乡间生活。
senses.why: An older branch turned the outward push inward: what one reaches for with pleasure is what one affects.
senses.whyCN: 一条更早的支线把向外的推及转向内：一个人乐于伸手去取的东西，就是他所偏爱之物。

intro.en: Affect is built in Latin from ad- 'towards' and facere 'to do', and it shares that root with effect and affection.
intro.cn: affect 在拉丁语中由 ad-「朝向」与 facere「做」构成，与 effect、affection 共享同一词根。

items.en: facere meant 'to do, make', and supplied the core of a large Latin word family.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，为拉丁语一个庞大的词族提供了核心。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant 'to, towards', and it often fused with the following consonant.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向、朝」，常与后面的辅音黏合变形。

items.en: ad- plus facere gave afficere, 'to do something to someone, to influence or move'.
items.cn: ad- 与 facere 合成 afficere，意为「对某人做点什么、施加影响或触动」。

items.en: Old French affecter carried the Latin verb into French with the senses of influencing and pretending.
items.cn: 古法语 affecter 把这个拉丁动词带入法语，已带有「影响」与「假装」两种意味。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fourteenth century; the emotional and medical senses developed soon after.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个动词，情感义与医学义随即发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group contrasts the fac- family, especially effect; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of influence, emotion and pretence.
note.cn: 形近组对照 fac- 词族，尤其是 effect；近义组收表示影响、感动与假装的动词。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a result or a change produced; it shares the fac- root but is usually a noun, not a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结果、效果」；与本词共享 fac- 词根，但多作名词而非动词。

entries.definition: The past participle and adjective from affect, meaning influenced or, of behaviour, insincere.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的过去分词兼形容词，义为「受影响的」，指举止时则为「做作的」。

entries.definition: The present participle and adjective from affect, meaning emotionally moving.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的现在分词兼形容词，义为「感人至深的」。

entries.definition: A noun meaning fondness or tenderness, built on the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喜爱、柔情」，由同一拉丁动词构成。

entries.definition: To change how someone thinks or acts, often gradually; close to the first sense of affect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「影响」，常指逐渐改变他人的想法或行为，与 affect 第一义接近。

entries.definition: To cause a strong feeling, especially of sadness or sympathy; the everyday verb for the emotional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使感动」，尤指引起悲伤或同情，是情感义最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To behave as if something is true when it is not; the plain verb behind the pretence sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「假装」，指把不真实的事当作真实来表现，正是 affect 假装义的白话对应。

entries.definition: To impress or affect someone in a particular way, as in the phrase struck by the news.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「给……留下印象、触动」，如 struck by the news 中的用法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb afficere and the everyday pairs that keep affect and effect apart.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 afficere，以及区分 affect 与 effect 的日常口诀。

normal.en: ad- means towards and facere means do: afficere is to do something to something.
normal.cn: ad- 意为「朝向」，facere 意为「做」：afficere 就是对某物做点什么。

normal.en: Affect is mostly a verb; effect is mostly a noun.
normal.cn: affect 多作动词，effect 多作名词。

normal.en: A disease affects the lungs, while a drug has an effect on them.
normal.cn: 疾病侵袭肺部用 affect，药物对肺部产生作用则说 have an effect on。

normal.en: To affect an accent is to put one on like a coat.
normal.cn: affect an accent 就是像披上一件外套那样装出某种口音。

normal.en: The same verb gives affection and affectation, one warm and one false.
normal.cn: 同一个动词生出 affection 与 affectation，一个温情，一个虚假。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing lightly on a pendulum; the swing changes direction without any hit.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻轻按在摆锤上，摆动方向被改变，却没有受到撞击。

abstract.en: The same hand can press on a heart, and the change it leaves there is being moved.
abstract.cn: 同一只手也可以按在心上，它在心里留下的改变就是「被感动」。

abstract.en: Sometimes the hand merely paints a feeling on its own face, and that is pretending.
abstract.cn: 有时这只手只是在自己脸上画一种表情，那就是假装。

examples.en: Rising prices affect every family in the town.
examples.cn: 物价上涨影响着镇上的每一个家庭。

examples.en: Her letter affected him more than he admitted.
examples.cn: 她的信对他的触动比他承认的更深。

examples.en: He affected indifference when the plan was rejected.
examples.cn: 计划被否决时，他装出一副无所谓的样子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额费克特」——额前被轻轻一推，方向就变了：影响

root: 拉丁语 afficere 由 ad-「向、朝」+ facere「做」构成，意为「对某人或某物做点什么、施加作用」。古法语 affecter 把它带入英语，由「施加作用」发展出「影响、感动、假装、侵袭」等义；更早的印欧来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of affect all describe one push onto something: a situation changed, feelings touched, a manner put on, a body part attacked, and an old fondness.
sensesIntro.cn: affect 的五个义项都描述同一股落到对象身上的推力：情况被改变、情感被触动、举止被装出、身体被侵袭，以及旧义中的偏爱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand presses lightly on an object and changes the way it moves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手轻按在某个对象上，改变了它的运动方式。

branches.en: THE CHANGE: a push on a situation alters what happens next.
branches.cn: 改变线：落在情况上的推力改变了接下来的走向。

branches.en: THE HEART: the same push reaches the feelings and leaves them stirred.
branches.cn: 情感线：同一股推力抵达情感，让它被搅动。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: the push is applied to one's own manner, producing a performance.
branches.cn: 表层线：推力被施加到自己的举止上，产生一场表演。

branches.en: THE BODY: a disease is an outside force that pushes into an organ.
branches.cn: 身体线：疾病是一股推入器官的外来力量。

branches.en: THE OLD LIKING: an older branch turns the reach inward as fondness.
branches.cn: 旧义线：更早的支线把伸出的手转向内，成为偏爱。

intro.en: Affect is a Latin verb formed from a directional prefix and the verb 'to do'; English adds its ordinary endings.
intro.cn: affect 是由方向前缀与表示「做」的动词构成的拉丁动词，英语再在其上加普通词尾。

latinIntro.en: Afficere, affectus and affectio are all recorded Latin forms, so no reconstruction is needed here.
latinIntro.cn: afficere、affectus 与 affectio 都是有记录的拉丁词形，此处无需重构。

items.example: It directs the action at an object.
items.exampleCN: 它把动作指向某个对象。
facere 提供这个动词的核心。

items.example: It is the direct source of affect.
items.exampleCN: 它是 affect 的直接来源。

items.example: It carries the family in English.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语中承载这一词族。

definition_zh: 喜爱；钟爱；感情；疾患（医学旧义）；影响（古义）
definition_en: a feeling of fondness or tender attachment towards a person or thing, or, in older medical use, a diseased condition
core_image: 心里被轻轻触动后留下的一股暖意，总朝着某个人
scene: 老人独居多年，唯一陪着他的是那条瘸腿的老狗，两者之间早已生出深厚的情意。She felt deep affection for the old dog.
sceneCN: 这里 affection 是「喜爱、钟爱」（第 1 个义项：对人或物的深厚情意）；句意为她对那条老狗怀有很深的感情。

pos.zh: 名词：喜爱；钟爱；感情；疾患（旧义）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「深情的；表示亲爱的」，语义从「情意」偏移为「流露情意的」
由 affectionate 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「深情地」，语义从「深情的」偏移为「以深情的方式」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「不满；离心」，语义从「情意」偏移为「情意被抽走」

senses.title: Fondness for a person or thing
senses.definition: a feeling of fondness, tenderness or attachment towards someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物怀有的喜爱、温柔或依恋之情
senses.example: He spoke of his old school with real affection.
senses.exampleCN: 他谈起自己的母校时满怀深情。
senses.why: Latin afficere meant to touch or move; affection is the warm state left in someone after being touched.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 afficere 意为「触动」，affection 就是一个人被触动后留在心里的那股暖意。

senses.title: A tender feeling or emotion
senses.definition: a feeling or emotion, especially one of warmth or tenderness, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 一种情感，尤指温暖、温柔之情，常用复数
senses.example: Her affections were divided between the two towns.
senses.exampleCN: 她对两座城镇各有一份情意。
senses.why: If one touch leaves warmth, many touches leave a set of feelings, and the plural affections names them together.
senses.whyCN: 一次触动留下暖意，多次触动就留下了一组情感，复数 affections 把它们合在一起称呼。

senses.title: A diseased condition, in old medicine
senses.definition: a diseased or abnormal condition of the body or mind, a medical use now largely obsolete
senses.definitionCN: 身体或精神的病态、异常状况，属今已基本废弃的医学用法
senses.example: The old medical text lists affections of the chest.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧医书列出了胸部的一些疾患。
senses.why: A disease also acts on the body, so the state it leaves behind was once called an affection.
senses.whyCN: 疾病同样作用于身体，它留下的状态在旧医学里也被称为 affection。

senses.title: Influence, in older usage
senses.definition: the action of one thing on another, an old sense close to the modern word influence
senses.definitionCN: 一物对另一物的作用，属接近现代 influence 的古义
senses.example: Old writers spoke of the affection of the moon on the tides.
senses.exampleCN: 古代作者谈到月亮对潮汐的影响。
senses.why: Before the word settled on feelings, it named any state produced by an outside force, including influence.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词固定指情感之前，它泛指外因造成的任何状态，其中也包括「影响」。

intro.en: Affection is the noun of the Latin verb afficere, 'to do something to', and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: affection 是拉丁动词 afficere「对……施加作用」的名词形式，经由法语进入英语。

items.en: facere meant 'to do, make' and formed the core of the family.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，构成这个词族的核心。

items.en: ad- plus facere gave afficere, 'to act on someone, to move them'.
items.cn: ad- 与 facere 合成 afficere，意为「作用于某人、触动某人」。

items.en: affectio named the state produced by that action, whether of body or of mind.
items.cn: affectio 指这种作用造成的状态，无论身体的还是心灵的。

items.en: Old French afection carried the noun into English with the feeling sense already leading.
items.cn: 古法语 afection 把这个名词带入英语，情感义当时已占主导。

items.en: The word is recorded from the thirteenth century; the medical and influence senses faded later.
items.cn: 这个词自十三世纪有记录，医学义与「影响」义后来逐渐消失。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the affec- family; the near-meaning group gathers words for fondness and emotional attachment.
note.cn: 形近组收 affec- 词族的词；近义组收表示喜爱与情感依恋的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning showing fondness or tenderness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「深情的、表示亲爱的」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a loving or tender way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「深情地」，由 affectionate 加后缀构成。

entries.definition: A noun meaning behaviour that is deliberately unnatural or pretentious; it shares the root but not the warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「做作、装腔作势」，与本词同根，却不含温情。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning insincere in manner, or influenced by something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「做作的」或「受影响的」，与本词同出 afficere。

entries.definition: A gentle liking for someone or something; the plainest noun for the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喜爱」，是第一义最直白的对应词。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of deep attachment; warmer and stronger than affection.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「爱」，比 affection 更热烈、更强烈。

entries.definition: Gentle, caring feeling towards someone; close to the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「温柔、柔情」，与第二义接近。

entries.definition: Any strong feeling such as joy, anger or fear; much broader than affection.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「情感、情绪」，范围比 affection 宽得多。

entries.definition: A feeling that binds one to a person or place; often built over time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「依恋」，指把人与人或地方系在一起的情感，常随时间积累。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb and the words that grew from it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁动词，以及由它生长出来的词。

normal.en: afficere is to touch or move: affection is the warmth left after that touch.
normal.cn: afficere 是「触动」：affection 就是触动之后留下的暖意。

normal.en: Affectionate adds -ate to make the adjective, and -ly makes the adverb.
normal.cn: 加 -ate 成形容词 affectionate，再加 -ly 成副词 affectionately。

normal.en: Affectation looks like the same word but means behaviour put on for show.
normal.cn: affectation 看起来同源，意思却是为表演而装出的举止。

normal.en: Have an affection for and win someone's affection are the two everyday patterns.
normal.cn: have an affection for 与 win someone's affection 是两个最日常的搭配模式。

normal.en: The plural affections often names a person's feelings taken as a group.
normal.cn: 复数 affections 常把一个人的种种情感合起来称呼。

abstract.en: Picture a hand resting on a shoulder for a moment, then leaving a warm print behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在肩上轻轻停留片刻，走后留下一个温暖的印子。

abstract.en: The same print appears on things as well as people: a house, a town, an old dog.
abstract.cn: 同一个印子也会落在物上而不只是人身上：一座房子、一座小镇、一条老狗。

abstract.en: Older books used the same word for illness and influence, because both are states left by something acting on you.
abstract.cn: 较早的书里，同一个词也指疾病与影响，因为两者都是外物作用于你之后留下的状态。

examples.en: She has a warm affection for her childhood village.
examples.cn: 她对童年的村庄怀有温暖的眷恋。

examples.en: He showed his affection by cooking for the whole family.
examples.cn: 他通过为全家做饭来表达自己的爱意。

examples.en: The two sisters were united by deep affection.
examples.cn: 深厚的感情把两姐妹连在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿费克申」——阿婆心口一阵暖，向着一处去：喜爱

root: 拉丁语 affectio 来自动词 afficere（ad-「向」+ facere「做」），本指「施加作用后留下的状态」，既可指身体病变，也可指心中被触动的情意。古法语 afection 把它带入英语，情感义逐渐成为主义；更早的印欧来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of affection all describe a state left by something acting on you: fondness, tender feeling, an old word for illness, and an old word for influence.
sensesIntro.cn: affection 的四个义项都指外物作用于你之后留下的状态：喜爱、情意、指疾病的旧义，以及指影响的古义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand rests briefly on a shoulder and leaves a warm print.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在肩上短暂停留，留下一个温暖的印子。

branches.en: THE WARMTH: the touch leaves fondness for a particular person or thing.
branches.cn: 暖意线：这次触动留下对某人某物的喜爱。

branches.en: THE FEELINGS: many touches gather into a set of tender emotions.
branches.cn: 情感线：多次触动聚成一组温柔的情感。

branches.en: THE BODY: an illness is also a state left by something acting on the body.
branches.cn: 身体线：疾病也是外物作用于身体后留下的状态。

branches.en: THE OLD FORCE: older texts used the word for any influence at all.
branches.cn: 旧义线：较早的文本用这个词泛指任何影响。

branches.en: THE CORE: both main senses keep the same warm print, one for a thing, one for a set of feelings.
branches.cn: 核心线：两个主义都保留同一个温暖印子，一个落在物上，一个落在情感上。

intro.en: Affection is a Latin noun built from a prefix, a verb and a noun ending; English adds the usual family suffixes.
intro.cn: affection 是由前缀、动词与名词词尾构成的拉丁名词；英语再普通后缀扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Afficere, affectio and affectus are all recorded, so the family needs no reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: afficere、affectio 与 affectus 均有记录，这个词族无需重构。

It is the source of affection.
