items.exampleCN: 它是直接的拉丁语祖先。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from ad- plus facere

definition_zh: 负担得起；抽得出（时间）；提供；给予；承受（后果）
definition_en: to have enough money, time or strength for something, or to provide or bear something
core_image: 口袋或日程里还能腾出一点余地，把事情接住
scene: 修车铺的师傅报出价钱，年轻人摸了摸口袋，犹豫着没有立刻点头。He could not afford the repairs this month.
sceneCN: 这里 afford 是「负担得起」（第 1 个义项：有钱支付某笔费用）；句意为这个月他付不起修车费。

pos.zh: 动词：负担得起；抽得出；提供；承受

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「负担得起的；价格合理的」，语义从「拿得出」偏移为「值得且拿得出」
由 affordable 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可负担性」，语义从「买得起」偏移为「价格是否可承受」
由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「可供性；可用线索」，语义从「提供」偏移为「环境提供的行动可能」

senses.title: To have enough money for something
senses.definition: to have enough money to pay for something without difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 有足够的钱支付某物而不致困难
senses.example: We cannot afford a new car this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年我们买不起新车。
senses.why: Old English aforthian meant to be able to carry something out; money is the first resource that decides whether one can.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 aforthian 意为「能够办成」，而钱是最先决定一个人能否办成的那项资源。

senses.title: To have enough time for something
senses.definition: to be able to spare the time or effort needed for something
senses.definitionCN: 能够腾出做某事所需的时间或精力
senses.example: She could not afford the time for a long meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她抽不出时间开长会。
senses.why: The same idea of having enough room extends from money to time and energy.
senses.whyCN: 「有余地」这层意思从钱扩展到时间与精力：有余地才腾得出来。

senses.title: To provide or give something
senses.definition: of a thing or situation, to offer or provide something valuable such as a view, chance or protection
senses.definitionCN: 指某物或某种情况提供有价值的视野、机会或保护等
senses.example: The wide windows afford a fine view of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 宽大的窗户提供了山谷的美丽景色。
senses.why: A thing that 'gives forth' a view or a chance is literally putting it within reach, which is what afford means.
senses.whyCN: 能「给出」景色或机会的东西，实际上是把它们放到你够得着的地方，这正是 afford 的本义。

senses.title: To bear the cost or risk of something
senses.definition: to be able to bear the cost, risk or consequences of an action, often in the negative
senses.definitionCN: 能够承担某一行为的代价、风险或后果，常用于否定
senses.example: No one can afford to ignore these warnings.
senses.exampleCN: 谁都承受不起忽视这些警告的后果。
senses.why: If one cannot carry the cost, one cannot afford it; the word moves from paying to bearing any burden.
senses.whyCN: 若一个人担不起代价，就是 afford 不起；这个词于是从付钱扩展到承担任何负担。

intro.en: Afford is not a Latin word at all: it comes from Old English and is related to forth, 'forward, onward'.
intro.cn: afford 根本不是拉丁词：它来自古英语，与表示「向前」的 forth 相关。

items.en: forth meant 'forward, onward, out', and it still survives in English today.
items.cn: forth 意为「向前、向外」，至今仍留在英语里。

items.en: aforthian meant 'to accomplish, provide, be able to carry out'.
items.cn: aforthian 意为「完成、供给、能够办成」。

items.en: The verb passed into Middle English as afforthen, still meaning to manage or provide.
items.cn: 这个动词进入中古英语作 afforthen，仍表示「办得到、供给」。

items.en: The modern spelling afford appears; the money sense becomes dominant and the older 'provide' sense narrows.
items.cn: 现代拼写 afford 出现，金钱义成为主流，较早的「提供」义收窄。

items.en: Afford spreads to time, opportunity and risk, always keeping the idea of having enough room.
items.cn: afford 扩展到时间、机会与风险，始终保留「有余地」的观念。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built directly on afford; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of managing, sparing and providing.
note.cn: 形近组收直接由 afford 构成的词；近义组收表示设法、腾出与提供的动词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning cheap enough to be paid for.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负担得起的」，由本词加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: The noun for how far something can be paid for by ordinary people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可负担性」，由 affordable 加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: A quality of an object that suggests how it can be used.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可供性」，指物件暗示其用法的那种特性。

entries.definition: To find a way to do something despite limits; close to the time and money senses.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「设法做到」，指在限制之下仍办成某事，与金钱、时间义接近。

entries.definition: To give up or make available something such as time or money.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「腾出、抽出」，指让出时间或金钱，与「抽得出时间」义接近。

entries.definition: To give or supply something needed; the plain verb behind the providing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提供、供给」，正是 afford 提供义的白话对应。

entries.definition: To accept or carry a cost, burden or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担、忍受」，指承受代价、负担或艰难，与第四义接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English verb and the phrases afford actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的古英语动词，以及 afford 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Forth means forward: aforthian is to push a thing through and get it done.
normal.cn: forth 意为「向前」：aforthian 就是把事情推过去、办成。

normal.en: Afford keeps the picture of having room left in the pocket or the day.
normal.cn: afford 保留着口袋或日程里还留有余地的画面。

normal.en: Can afford to is the everyday frame for money, time and risk alike.
normal.cn: can afford to 是钱、时间与风险通用的日常句式。

normal.en: Affordable adds -able, so the word turns from ability into price.
normal.cn: affordable 加 -able，词义从「有能力」转为「价格可承受」。

normal.en: The older sense 'to provide' survives in phrases such as afford a view.
normal.cn: 较早的「提供」义仍留在 afford a view 这类短语里。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching into a pocket and finding a little space still there.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸进口袋，发现里面还留着一点空隙。

abstract.en: The same space can be a free hour, a chance offered, or the strength to take a risk.
abstract.cn: 同一片空隙可以是一个空闲的小时、一个被给的机会，或承担风险的力量。

abstract.en: Afford always asks one question: is there enough room to take this on?
abstract.cn: afford 始终在问同一个问题：还有没有余地接下这件事？

examples.en: They saved for years so they could afford a small flat.
examples.cn: 他们攒了好几年钱，才买得起一套小公寓。

examples.en: I can hardly afford to take a week off work.
examples.cn: 我几乎抽不出一周的时间离开工作。

examples.en: The hilltop affords a clear view of the whole bay.
examples.cn: 山顶上可以看到整个海湾的清晰景色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿福德」——阿福口袋还有余地，什么都办得成：负担得起

root: 古英语 aforthian 意为「完成、供给、能够办成」，由 forth「向前」加动词前缀构成；中古英语作 afforthen，现代拼写定为 afford。词义由「办得到」扩展为「负担得起、抽得出、提供、承受」；它属日耳曼语词，拉丁语中没有同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of afford all ask whether there is enough room: money to pay, time to spare, value a thing offers, and strength to bear a risk.
sensesIntro.cn: afford 的四个义项都在问有没有余地：钱够不够付、时间腾不腾得出、某物能提供什么，以及力量够不够承担风险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand finds a little space left in a pocket or in a day.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在口袋或一天里找到还剩下的一点空隙。

branches.en: THE PURSE: the first room to check is the money available.
branches.cn: 钱包线：最先要看的余地是手头的钱。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: the same room is measured in hours and energy.
branches.cn: 时间线：同一片余地也用小时与精力来衡量。

branches.en: THE GIFT: a thing with room to give offers a view, a chance or protection.
branches.cn: 给予线：有余地给出的东西会提供视野、机会或保护。

branches.en: THE BURDEN: what can be carried can also be borne as cost or risk.
branches.cn: 承担线：担得起的东西也能作为代价或风险被承受。

branches.en: THE CORE: money and time are the two everyday forms of having enough room.
branches.cn: 核心线：钱与时间是「有余地」最常见的两种形态。

intro.en: Afford is a native English verb, not a Latin construction; its parts are an old adverb of direction and verbal endings.
intro.cn: afford 是英语本土动词，不是拉丁式构造；其成分是一个古老的方向副词与动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Afford has no recorded Latin cognate, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: afford 没有可考的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁同族一栏留空。

items.example: Forth still appears in set phrases.
items.exampleCN: forth 仍出现在固定短语中。

items.example: It is the earliest recorded form of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个动词最早有记录的形式。

items.example: It is the Middle English spelling.

items.meaning: to be able to pay for or bear

definition_zh: 害怕的；担心的；恐怕（礼貌用语）；不敢
definition_en: feeling fear or worry, politely announcing bad news, or unwilling to do something because of fear
core_image: 心口一紧，脚往后缩，想躲开眼前的东西
scene: 深夜的走廊灯坏了，小女孩紧紧抓着母亲的衣角，不肯往前迈步。The little girl was afraid to walk on alone.
sceneCN: 这里 afraid 是「不敢」（第 4 个义项：因为害怕而不愿做某事）；句意为小女孩不敢独自往前走。

pos.zh: 形容词：害怕的；担心的；恐怕；不敢（只作表语）

derivatives.zh: 由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「不怕的；无畏的」，语义从「害怕」偏移为「无所畏惧」
与本词同出古法语 esfreer 的名词，义为「斗殴；骚乱」，语义从「受惊」偏移为「当众的冲突」

senses.title: Feeling fear of something
senses.definition: feeling fear because of a person, thing or situation that seems dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 因为某人、某物或某种情况看起来危险而感到恐惧
senses.example: The child is afraid of thunder.
senses.exampleCN: 这个孩子害怕打雷。
senses.why: The word began as a participle meaning 'frightened', so its oldest sense is the state of being scared.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是意为「被吓到」的分词，所以最早的义项就是受惊的状态。

senses.title: Worried about something
senses.definition: worried that something bad may happen or may have happened
senses.definitionCN: 担心坏事可能发生或已经发生
senses.example: She was afraid that the letter had been lost.
senses.exampleCN: 她担心那封信已经丢失了。
senses.why: Fear need not have an enemy in sight; it can also be a quiet worry about what might come.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧不一定有看得见的敌人，它也可以是对可能发生之事的一种安静担忧。

senses.title: I'm afraid: a polite apology
senses.definition: used in the phrase I'm afraid to say politely that something bad is true or that one must refuse
senses.definitionCN: 用于 I'm afraid 这一说法，礼貌地表示坏消息属实或必须拒绝
senses.example: I'm afraid the train has already left.
senses.exampleCN: 恐怕火车已经开走了。
senses.why: The speaker softens bad news by naming a small fear, as if apologising for the discomfort it causes.
senses.whyCN: 说话人先承认一点「怕」，用这种方式冲淡坏消息带来的不适，等于为冒犯致歉。

senses.title: Unwilling to do something because of fear
senses.definition: unwilling to do something because one is frightened of the result
senses.definitionCN: 因为害怕结果而不愿意做某事
senses.example: He was afraid to speak in front of the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他不敢在全班面前发言。
senses.why: When fear stands in front of an action, the adjective moves from the feeling to the refusal it causes.
senses.whyCN: 当恐惧挡在动作前面，这个形容词就从「感受」转向它造成的「拒绝」。

intro.en: Afraid is a worn-down past participle of an old French verb meaning 'to frighten'.
intro.cn: afraid 是一个古法语动词「使惊恐」的过去分词，经过长期磨损而成。

items.en: esfreer meant 'to frighten, to alarm', and its deeper Latin source is uncertain.
items.cn: esfreer 意为「使惊恐、使惊慌」，其更早的拉丁来源不确定。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the verb as affraien, 'to frighten or disturb'.
items.cn: 中古英语借入这个动词作 affraien，意为「使惊恐、使不安」。

items.en: The past participle affraid or affraied described someone who had been frightened.
items.cn: 过去分词 affraid 或 affraied 描述一个已经被吓到的人。

items.en: The participle became an adjective; the spelling settled as afraid and the verb faded.
items.cn: 这个分词变成形容词，拼写定为 afraid，原来的动词则逐渐消失。

items.en: The adjective gained the polite phrase I'm afraid and the pattern afraid to do.
items.cn: 这个形容词发展出礼貌语 I'm afraid 与 afraid to do 的句式。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same frightening verb; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of fear with different strength.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「使惊恐」动词的词；近义组收表示恐惧的形容词，强度各不相同。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a noisy fight in a public place, from the same Old French verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「斗殴、骚乱」，与本词同出那个古法语动词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning not frightened at all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不怕的、无畏的」，由本词加否定前缀构成。

entries.definition: An old or dialect form of afraid, now rare in standard English.
entries.definitionCN: afraid 的古老或方言形式，义为「害怕的」，现代标准英语中已罕见。

entries.definition: Frightened, especially of something immediate; more informal than afraid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「害怕的」，多指眼前的恐惧，比 afraid 更口语。

entries.definition: Made afraid by something that has happened or is happening.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受惊的」，指被已发生或正发生的事吓到。

entries.definition: Feeling fear, or causing fear; more formal and often literary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「害怕的」或「可怕的」，较正式，带文学色彩。

entries.definition: Extremely frightened; much stronger than afraid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「极度恐惧的」，程度远强于 afraid。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old French verb behind the word and the patterns it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词背后真实的古法语动词，以及它出现的句式。

normal.en: esfreer means to frighten: afraid is the state of having been frightened.
normal.cn: esfreer 意为「使惊恐」：afraid 就是被吓到之后的状态。

normal.en: The -ed ending is a worn participle, which is why afraid only works after a linking verb.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ed 是磨损的过去分词，所以 afraid 只能放在系动词之后作表语。

normal.en: Afraid of names the thing, afraid to names the action one avoids.
normal.cn: afraid of 后接名词，afraid to 后接不敢做的动作。

normal.en: I'm afraid is not a confession of fear but a polite way to soften bad news.
normal.cn: I'm afraid 并不是承认害怕，而是冲淡坏消息的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Affray is the old noun from the same verb, meaning a public disturbance.
normal.cn: affray 是同一动词留下的旧名词，意为当众骚乱。

abstract.en: Picture a child at the top of dark stairs, one foot lifted but not set down.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子站在黑漆漆的楼梯口，一只脚抬起来却不敢落下。

abstract.en: The lifted foot can freeze before a storm, before a crowd, or before a piece of news.
abstract.cn: 这只抬起的脚可以在雷雨前、在人群前、在一条消息前停住。

abstract.en: The same lifted foot also appears in polite talk, where fear is only a small bow of apology.
abstract.cn: 同一只抬起的脚也出现在礼貌用语里，那里的「怕」只是一次小小的道歉鞠躬。

examples.en: Most small children are afraid of the dark.
examples.cn: 大多数幼儿都怕黑。

examples.en: I'm afraid we have missed the last bus.
examples.cn: 恐怕我们错过了末班车。

examples.en: She was afraid to tell her parents the truth.
examples.cn: 她不敢把真相告诉父母。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额弗雷德」——额头一凉，往后一缩：害怕

root: 中古英语 affraien 来自古法语 esfreer「使惊恐」，其过去分词 affraied 演变为形容词 afraid。更早的拉丁来源不确定，一般认为与通俗拉丁语中表示「使寒栗」的形式有关，但没有可靠记录的同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of afraid all start from the state of being frightened: fear of a thing, worry about what may come, a polite apology, and a refusal caused by fear.
sensesIntro.cn: afraid 的四个义项都从「被吓到」的状态出发：怕某物、担心可能发生的事、礼貌的道歉，以及因恐惧而拒绝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child's foot is lifted at the top of a dark stair and held there.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子在黑暗的楼梯口抬起一只脚，却停住不落。

branches.en: THE DANGER: fear is fixed on a thing that seems dangerous.
branches.cn: 危险线：恐惧固定在一个看起来危险的对象上。

branches.en: THE FUTURE: the same fear turns into worry about what may happen.
branches.cn: 未来说：同一种恐惧转为对可能发生之事的担忧。

branches.en: THE MANNER: in I'm afraid, fear becomes a small polite apology.
branches.cn: 礼貌线：在 I'm afraid 中，恐惧变成一句小小的礼貌道歉。

branches.en: THE STOP: fear placed before an action becomes a refusal to move.
branches.cn: 停步线：恐惧挡在动作之前，就成了拒绝迈步。

branches.en: THE BODY: the lifted foot is the core picture shared by real fear and the fear that stops an action.
branches.cn: 身体线：抬起的脚是真正的恐惧与阻止行动的恐惧共享的核心画面。

intro.en: Afraid is not built from living English affixes; it is a worn French participle, and its endings are historical traces.
intro.cn: afraid 不是由现代英语词缀构成的，它是一个磨损的法语分词，其词尾只是历史痕迹。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate of this French verb is securely recorded, so the Latin list is left empty; the deeper source is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个法语动词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，因此拉丁同族一栏留空；更早来源不确定。

items.example: It carries the sense of alarm.
Esfreer is the source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: esfreer 是英语这个词的来源。

items.example: It was borrowed in the fourteenth century.

items.exampleCN: 这个分词变成了形容词。

items.example: She was afraid of the dark.

items.exampleCN: 它标记古老的过去分词。

definition_zh: 在……之后（时间）；在……之后（顺序）；追赶；以……命名；终究；之后
definition_en: later than something in time or order, in pursuit of something, or in phrases expressing naming, cause and conclusion
core_image: 跟在某件事的后面，一步步追着它走
scene: 雨停之后，院子里积起一片片水洼，孩子们才敢跑出来玩。We went out to play after the rain stopped.
sceneCN: 这里 after 是「在……之后」（第 1 个义项：时间上晚于某事）；句意为雨停之后我们出去玩了。

pos.zh: 介词：在……之后；在……后面；追赶；以……命名
副词：之后；在后面
连词：在……之后

derivatives.zh: 由 after 加后缀 -ward 构成，义为「后来」，语义从「在后面」偏移为「在时间上之后」
由 afterward 加副词后缀 -s 构成，义为「后来」，是英式更常见的变体
由 after 与 noon 复合，义为「下午」，语义从「在正午之后」凝固为一天中的时段
由 after 与 math「割草」复合，义为「后果；余波」，语义从「割草之后再长出的草」偏移为「事件之后的状态」

senses.title: Later than something in time
senses.definition: happening or existing later than a particular time, event or period
senses.definitionCN: 发生在某一时间、事件或时期之后，或存在于其后
senses.example: We went out to play after the rain stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 雨停之后我们出去玩了。
senses.why: Old English æfter meant 'behind, following'; a later time is simply the ground that lies behind the present point.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 æfter 意为「在后面、跟随」，较晚的时间正是位于当下这一点之后的地面。

senses.title: Later in order or rank
senses.definition: following something else in a sequence, list or order of importance
senses.definitionCN: 在序列、清单或重要性的次序上跟在某物之后
senses.example: The letter C comes after B.
senses.exampleCN: 字母 C 排在 B 之后。
senses.why: The same 'behind' picture works for a queue: what comes after stands behind what came before.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅「在后面」的画面也适用于队列：排在后面的东西站在前面的东西之后。

senses.title: In pursuit of someone or something
senses.definition: following or chasing someone or something in order to catch them
senses.definitionCN: 跟在某人或某物后面，为的是抓住它
senses.example: The dog ran after the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 那条狗追着球跑。
senses.why: A pursuer literally moves behind the fleeing thing, so after becomes the preposition of the chase.
senses.whyCN: 追赶者字面上就移动在被追之物的后面，于是 after 成了表示追逐的介词。

senses.title: Named in honour of someone
senses.definition: used after name or call to say that something takes its name from a person or place
senses.definitionCN: 用于 name 或 call 之后，表示某物取自某人或某地的名字
senses.example: The street was named after a local poet.
senses.exampleCN: 这条街以当地一位诗人的名字命名。
senses.why: A name that follows a person keeps that person behind it, so the thing is named after them.
senses.whyCN: 跟在某人之后的名字把那个人留在名字背后，所以事物是以他之后序位上的名字命名的。

senses.title: After all: in spite of everything
senses.definition: in the phrase after all, used to mean in spite of what happened, or for a reason one has just remembered
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 after all，表示尽管发生了这些事，或考虑到刚想起的理由
senses.example: After all, she had warned us about the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 毕竟她早就警告过我们有暴风雨。
senses.why: What comes after everything else is the final balance, and after all marks that last look at the whole.
senses.whyCN: 在一切之后到来的就是最终的结算，after all 标记的正是对整个局面的最后一瞥。

senses.title: Afterwards, as an adverb
senses.definition: used as an adverb to mean at a later time, without naming the earlier event
senses.definitionCN: 作副词使用，表示在较晚的时间，不点明较早的那件事
senses.example: He fell asleep soon after.
senses.exampleCN: 他不久之后就睡着了。
senses.why: Once the object is dropped, the word stands alone as an adverb and simply points to later time.
senses.whyCN: 一旦省去后面的对象，这个词就独立成副词，只指向较晚的时间。

intro.en: After is one of the oldest English words, a Germanic preposition related to of and with no Latin cognate.
intro.cn: after 是英语最古老的词之一，属日耳曼语介词，与 of 相关，没有拉丁同族词。

items.en: A Germanic form meaning 'behind, after' is reconstructed; its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语中有一个表示「在后面」的形式，确切形状不确定。

items.en: æfter meant 'behind, following, in pursuit of', and it governed the dative case.
items.cn: æfter 意为「在后面、跟随、追赶」，支配与格。

items.en: The spelling and pronunciation simplified, and the word took on its modern range of uses.
items.cn: 拼写与读音简化，这个词逐渐获得现代的各种用法。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as after all and named after took shape in Middle and early modern English.
items.cn: after all、named after 这类固定短语在中古英语与早期现代英语中成形。

items.en: After works as preposition, adverb and conjunction, and it also forms compounds such as afternoon.
items.cn: after 可作介词、副词与连词，还构成 afternoon 这类复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and derivatives built on after; the near-meaning group gathers words for what follows.
note.cn: 形近组收由 after 构成的复合词与派生词；近义组收表示「随后」的词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning at a later time, built on after plus -ward.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「后来」，由 after 加 -ward 构成。

entries.definition: The part of the day between noon and evening, from after plus noon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「下午」，由 after 与 noon 复合而成。

entries.definition: The consequences of a serious event, originally the grass growing after mowing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后果、余波」，原指割草之后再长出的草。

entries.definition: The British spelling of afterward, with the adverbial -s.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「后来」，是 afterward 的英式变体，带副词词尾 -s。

entries.definition: At the back of something; the spatial picture underneath the first sense of after.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……后面」，正是 after 第一义背后的空间画面。

entries.definition: Coming after something in time or order; close to the order sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或介词，义为「紧接着的、在……之后」，与顺序义接近。

entries.definition: From a past time until now; a time expression that overlaps with after.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或连词，义为「自从」，与 after 的时间义相交叠。

entries.definition: At a time after the present or after a stated time; the adverb of the time sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「后来、较晚」，是 after 时间义的副词对应。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English form and the fixed phrases after actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的古英语形式，以及 after 实际出现的固定短语。

normal.en: æfter meant behind: everything after comes behind the point you stand at.
normal.cn: æfter 意为「在后面」：所有在后的东西都位于你所站之点后面。

normal.en: After all is the last look taken after everything has happened.
normal.cn: after all 是事情全部发生之后所做的最后一瞥。

normal.en: Named after keeps the honoured person behind the name.
normal.cn: named after 把受纪念的人留在名字的背后。

normal.en: Look after is to keep your eyes on someone from behind and care for them.
normal.cn: look after 就是跟在后面照看、照料某人。

normal.en: After also builds compounds: afternoon, afterward, aftermath.
normal.cn: after 还构成复合词：afternoon、afterward、aftermath。

abstract.en: Picture a person walking a few steps behind a cart along a dusty road.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在有土的路上，跟在车子后面几步的地方走着。

abstract.en: The same following distance can be time, order, a chase, or a name carried in someone's honour.
abstract.cn: 同一段跟随的距离可以是时间、顺序、追逐，也可以是用来纪念某人的名字。

abstract.en: When the cart disappears, the walker still moves on, and the word becomes a bare adverb of later time.
abstract.cn: 车子消失后，走路的人仍在往前，这个词就变成只表示「后来」的副词。

examples.en: She arrived after midnight.
examples.cn: 她在午夜之后到达。

examples.en: The dog ran after the ball.
examples.cn: 那条狗追着球跑。

examples.en: The street was named after a local poet.
examples.cn: 这条街以当地一位诗人的名字命名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿福特」——跟在后面，特特地追上去：在……之后

root: 古英语 æfter「在后面、跟随、追赶」属日耳曼语介词，与 of 同源，拉丁语中没有对应同族词。词义由空间上的「在后面」扩展为时间与顺序上的「之后」，并发展出「追赶、以……命名、毕竟」等用法；更早的日耳曼语形式不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of after all keep something behind or following: later time, later order, a chase, a name in honour, a final reckoning, and a bare adverb for later.
sensesIntro.cn: after 的六个义项都保留「在后面、跟随」的意思：较晚的时间、较后的顺序、追逐、纪念之名、最终的结算，以及只表示「后来」的副词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker stays a few steps behind a moving cart.
core.cn: 核心意象：走路的人始终跟在移动的车子后面几步。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: what is behind in space becomes later in time.
branches.cn: 时间线：空间上在后，转为时间上较晚。

branches.en: THE QUEUE: the same position becomes a place in a sequence.
branches.cn: 顺序线：同一位置变成序列中的一个位次。

branches.en: THE CHASE: following behind turns into running after something.
branches.cn: 追逐线：跟在后面变成追赶某物。

branches.en: THE NAME: the honoured person stays behind the name given to a place.
branches.cn: 命名线：受纪念的人留在赐予某地的名字背后。

branches.en: THE LAST LOOK: after all weighs the whole, and the bare adverb points to later time.
branches.cn: 末视线：after all 权衡全局，单独的副词则指向较晚的时间。

intro.en: After is a native Germanic word; the affixes shown here are the pieces it combines with in English.
intro.cn: after 是本土日耳曼语词；这里列出的构词成分是它在英语中组合的对象。

latinIntro.en: After has no Latin cognate, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: after 没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁同族一栏留空。

items.example: It is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: 它是最早有记录的形式。
它构成 afternoon 与 aftermath。

items.example: Of is the old cousin of after.
items.exampleCN: of 是 after 的古老同族词。

definition_zh: 下午；午后；每个下午；下午好（问候语）
definition_en: the period of the day between noon and evening, or a greeting used during that period
core_image: 太阳越过正午最高点后，慢慢向西斜的那一段时光
scene: 夏天的太阳偏到西边，老人们搬着竹椅到院子里乘凉。We sat under the tree all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 afternoon 是「下午」（第 1 个义项：正午到傍晚之间的时段）；句意为我们在树下坐了一整个下午。

pos.zh: 名词：下午；午后；每个下午；下午好

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 mid- 与 afternoon 复合，义为「下午中间时段」，语义从「下午」收窄为中段
由本词加副词属格 -s 构成，义为「每个下午；下午时段的惯常」，语义从时段偏移为反复
由 afternoon 与 tea 复合，义为「下午茶」，语义从时段偏移为在该时段的固定活动

senses.title: The period between noon and evening
senses.definition: the part of the day that begins after noon and ends towards evening
senses.definitionCN: 从正午之后开始、到接近傍晚结束的一天中的一段
senses.example: The afternoon was hot and still.
senses.exampleCN: 那个下午又热又静。
senses.why: The word is simply after plus noon: the whole stretch that follows the noon mark takes its name from that position.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 after 加 noon：正午这个刻度之后的一整段，直接借用了「在正午之后」这个位置来命名。

senses.title: Every afternoon, as a repeated time
senses.definition: used in the plural or as an adverb to mean on every afternoon or during afternoons generally
senses.definitionCN: 用复数或作副词，表示每个下午或在下午这段时间里惯常如此
senses.example: She works afternoons at the corner shop.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天下午在街角的小店干活。
senses.why: Adding -s turns one named period into a repeated one, so the time word begins to mean every such period.
senses.whyCN: 加上 -s 把一个有名字的时段变成反复出现的时段，于是这个时间词开始表示「每个这样的时段」。

senses.title: Good afternoon: a daytime greeting
senses.definition: used in the fixed greeting good afternoon, said when people meet during the afternoon
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定问候语 good afternoon，在下午见面时使用
senses.example: Good afternoon, madam, may I help you?
senses.exampleCN: 下午好，女士，需要帮忙吗？
senses.why: A named span of the day can stand for the greeting spoken inside it, so the period itself becomes a polite hello.
senses.whyCN: 一天中一个有名字的时段可以代表在该时段说出的问候，于是这段时间本身变成了一句礼貌的你好。

intro.en: Afternoon is an English compound of after and noon, and noon itself comes from Latin for the ninth hour.
intro.cn: afternoon 是 after 与 noon 的英语复合词，而 noon 本身出自拉丁语「第九小时」的说法。

items.en: nona hora meant 'the ninth hour' of the Roman day, roughly mid-afternoon.
items.cn: nona hora 意为罗马白天的「第九小时」，大致在午后。

items.en: Old English non borrowed the church sense and named the hour of prayer around mid-afternoon.
items.cn: 古英语 non 借入教会的用法，指午后祈祷的那个时辰。

items.en: The meaning of noon shifted forward to the middle of the day, the modern sense.
items.cn: noon 的词义前移，固定为一天的正中，即现代意义。

items.en: After and noon were joined as a compound naming the stretch following midday.
items.cn: after 与 noon 组合成复合词，命名正午之后的那一段。

items.en: Afternoon gained the greeting good afternoon and the repeated adverbial use afternoons.
items.cn: afternoon 发展出问候语 good afternoon 与副词性的 afternoons 用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noon family and compounds; the near-meaning group gathers other parts of the day.
note.cn: 形近组收 noon 词族与复合词；近义组收一天中的其他时段。

entries.definition: The plural of afternoon, also used adverbially for every afternoon.
entries.definitionCN: afternoon 的复数形式，也作副词表示「每个下午」。

entries.definition: The middle part of the afternoon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「下午中段」，由 mid- 与 afternoon 复合。

entries.definition: Twelve o'clock in the day; the second element of afternoon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「正午」，是 afternoon 的第二成分。

entries.definition: The first element of the compound, meaning later than.
entries.definitionCN: afternoon 的第一成分，义为「在……之后」。

entries.definition: The part of the day after the afternoon and before night.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「傍晚、晚上」，是下午之后、夜晚之前的一段。

entries.definition: The middle of the day, around twelve o'clock; where the afternoon begins.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「正午」，是下午开始的地方。

entries.definition: The part of the day before noon; the counterpart on the other side of midday.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「上午」，与 afternoon 分居正午两侧。

entries.definition: The time when daylight fades, at the end of the afternoon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黄昏」，是下午结束时日光渐暗的那一刻。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real parts of the compound and the phrases afternoon appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个复合词真实的两部分，以及 afternoon 出现的搭配。

normal.en: After plus noon: the afternoon is literally the time after midday.
normal.cn: after 加 noon：下午字面上就是正午之后的时间。

normal.en: Noon comes from Latin nona hora, the ninth hour of the Roman day.
normal.cn: noon 来自拉丁语 nona hora，即罗马白天的第九小时。

normal.en: Good afternoon is the greeting that borrows the name of the period.
normal.cn: good afternoon 是借用了这段时间名称的问候语。

normal.en: Afternoons with -s means every afternoon, a repeated span.
normal.cn: afternoons 带 -s，表示每个下午，是反复出现的时段。

normal.en: Afternoon tea and afternoon nap name activities fixed inside the period.
normal.cn: afternoon tea 与 afternoon nap 命名固定在这段时间里的活动。

abstract.en: Picture the sun passing its highest point and beginning to lean towards the west.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳越过最高点，开始向西倾斜。

abstract.en: The long slope of light after that point is the afternoon, a stretch rather than a moment.
abstract.cn: 那个点之后长长的一段斜光就是下午，是一段而非一刻。

abstract.en: The same stretch can be repeated as afternoons, or spoken as a greeting when two people meet inside it.
abstract.cn: 同一段时光可以复数为 afternoons，也可以在两人相遇时化作一句问候。

examples.en: We spent the whole afternoon by the river.
examples.cn: 我们在河边度过了整个下午。

examples.en: Good afternoon, everyone; the meeting will begin in a moment.
examples.cn: 大家下午好，会议马上开始。

examples.en: He often naps afternoons during the summer.
examples.cn: 夏天他常常在下午小睡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿夫特努恩」——午后太阳慢慢斜，阿婆搬椅到院中

root: afternoon 由 after「在……之后」与 noon「正午」复合而成。noon 源自古英语 non，出自拉丁语 nona hora「第九小时」，原指午后祈祷的时辰，后来词义前移固定为正午。整个复合词义为「正午之后的一段时光」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of afternoon all name the stretch after midday: the period itself, the repeated every-afternoon use, and the greeting spoken inside it.
sensesIntro.cn: afternoon 的三个义项都指正午之后的那一段：时段本身、反复的「每个下午」，以及在这段时间里说出的问候。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sun passes its highest point and begins leaning west.
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳越过最高点，开始向西倾斜。

branches.en: THE PERIOD: the stretch after midday is named directly from its position.
branches.cn: 时段线：正午之后的一段直接按它的位置命名。

branches.en: THE REPETITION: the same span repeats as every afternoon.
branches.cn: 反复线：同一段时光反复出现，成为「每个下午」。

branches.en: THE GREETING: the name of the span becomes a polite hello.
branches.cn: 问候线：这段时间的名称变成一句礼貌的你好。

branches.en: THE CORE: one named span can be counted once or repeated day after day.
branches.cn: 核心线：同一个有名字的时段，可以只算一次，也可以日复一日重复。

branches.en: THE LIGHT: the long afternoon light is also the setting of the greeting.
branches.cn: 光线段：下午漫长的光也是问候发生的背景。

intro.en: Afternoon is an English compound; its two halves are native or borrowed words that also build other compounds.
intro.cn: afternoon 是英语复合词，它的两半都是可以再构成其他复合词的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nona and hora are recorded, and nona hora is the phrase behind noon.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nona 与 hora 均有记录，nona hora 正是 noon 背后的短语。

items.example: It is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个复合词的前一半。

items.example: It is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个复合词的后一半。

items.example: Nona hora meant the ninth hour.
items.exampleCN: nona hora 意为第九小时。

definition_zh: 后来；之后；事后
definition_en: at a later time, after something else has happened or in the order that follows
core_image: 一件事过去以后，脚步才转向下一段
scene: 会议散了，人们陆续离开，只有他还站在原地，想着刚才那句没说完的话。Shortly afterward, he left the hall alone.
sceneCN: 这里 afterward 是「后来」（第 1 个义项：在较早的事情之后的时间里）；句意为不久之后他独自离开了大厅。

pos.zh: 副词：后来；之后；事后

derivatives.zh: 由 afterward 加副词词尾 -s 构成，义为「后来」，是英式英语更常见的变体
由 after 与 word 复合，义为「后记；跋」，与 afterward 拼写相近但意义不同

senses.title: At a later time
senses.definition: at a time later than the event just mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 在刚才提到的那件事之后的时间里
senses.example: He moved to the city and married soon afterward.
senses.exampleCN: 他搬到城里，不久之后就结了婚。
senses.why: After means behind and -ward means towards, so afterward points the mind towards what lies behind the present event.
senses.whyCN: after 意为「在后面」，-ward 意为「朝向」，合起来就是把心思朝当下事件之后的方向指。

senses.title: Next in order
senses.definition: in the order that follows, as the next step or item in a sequence
senses.definitionCN: 按随后的次序，作为序列中的下一步或下一项
senses.example: The guests arrived one after another and afterward came the speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 客人一个接一个到来，随后是致辞。
senses.why: The same 'towards what is behind' movement works for a sequence, where the next item stands behind the current one.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「朝向后方」的移动也适用于序列：下一项就站在当前项的后面。

senses.title: After the fact, in retrospect
senses.definition: after an event has ended, especially when looking back on it with new understanding
senses.definitionCN: 在一件事结束之后，尤指带着新的理解回望它时
senses.example: Afterward she realised how close they had come to disaster.
senses.exampleCN: 事后她才意识到他们离灾难有多近。
senses.why: Looking back is a movement of the mind towards what is already behind, exactly the direction the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 回望是心思朝已经落在后方的东西移动，正是这个词所描述的方向。

intro.en: Afterward is after plus the old suffix -ward, 'towards', and the British form adds an adverbial -s.
intro.cn: afterward 是 after 加古后缀 -ward「朝向」，英式形式再带一个副词词尾 -s。

items.en: -weard was a suffix meaning 'towards, in the direction of'.
items.cn: -weard 是表示「朝向、往……方向」的后缀。

items.en: æfter supplied the first half, meaning 'behind, after'.
items.cn: æfter 提供前半部分，意为「在后面、之后」。

items.en: The two parts joined as afterward, an adverb of later time.
items.cn: 两部分合成 afterward，成为表示较晚时间的副词。

items.en: The form afterwards with adverbial -s spread in Britain while afterward remained common in America.
items.cn: 带副词 -s 的 afterwards 在英国流行，afterward 则在美洲常用。

items.en: Afterward settled as the American spelling and afterwards as the British one.
items.cn: 现代英语中 afterward 固定为美式拼写，afterwards 为英式拼写。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the -ward family and a look-alike compound; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs for what comes next.
note.cn: 形近组收 -ward 词族与一个形近复合词；近义组收表示「随后」的副词。

entries.definition: The British variant of afterward, carrying an adverbial -s.
entries.definitionCN: afterward 的英式变体，带副词词尾 -s。

entries.definition: A short section at the end of a book; it is after plus word, not after plus -ward.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后记、跋」；它由 after 与 word 构成，并非 after 加 -ward，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: In the direction of something; built with the same -ward suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「朝向」，由同一个 -ward 后缀构成。

entries.definition: Towards the front or the future; another word made with -ward.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「向前」，同属 -ward 后缀构成的词。

entries.definition: At a time after now or after a stated time; the simplest synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「后来、较晚」，是最简单的同义词。

entries.definition: Afterwards, especially in a formal or written account.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「随后」，多用于正式或书面叙述。

entries.definition: At that time or next in order; shorter and less formal than afterward.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「那时、接着」，比 afterward 更短、更口语。

entries.definition: After that point, especially in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「此后」，多用于正式书面语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real suffix -ward and the pairs after and afterwards.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的后缀 -ward，以及 after 与 afterwards 的对应关系。

normal.en: -ward means towards: afterward is towards what lies behind the event.
normal.cn: -ward 意为「朝向」：afterward 就是朝事件之后的方向。

normal.en: Afterward is the American form; afterwards is the British form.
normal.cn: afterward 是美式形式，afterwards 是英式形式。

normal.en: Afterword is after plus word, a section at the end of a book, not a time word.
normal.cn: afterword 是 after 加 word，指书末的后记，不是时间词。

normal.en: Shortly afterward and soon afterward are the two most common frames.
normal.cn: shortly afterward 与 soon afterward 是两个最常见的框架。

normal.en: The word can point to a later time or to the next item in a sequence.
normal.cn: 这个词既能指向较晚的时间，也能指向序列中的下一项。

abstract.en: Picture a door closing behind a meeting and a person still standing in the empty room.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门在会议结束后关上，一个人还站在空房间里。

abstract.en: He turns towards that closed door only later, and that turn is the afterward.
abstract.cn: 他过一会儿才转向那扇关上的门，这一次转身就是 afterward。

abstract.en: Looking back on it much later, the same turn becomes a quiet moment of realising something.
abstract.cn: 很久以后再回望，同一次转身就成了安静地意识到某事的时刻。

examples.en: They met at a wedding and became friends afterward.
examples.cn: 他们在一次婚礼上相识，后来成了朋友。

examples.en: The storm passed, and afterward the streets were full of broken branches.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过去了，之后街上到处是断枝。

examples.en: Shortly afterward, the company announced its new plan.
examples.cn: 不久之后，公司宣布了新计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿夫特沃德」——事情过后，脚步才转向下一段

root: afterward 由 after「在后」与古英语后缀 -weard「朝向」合成，字面意为「朝后方」。副词 -s 加在词尾形成英式 afterwards。词义由空间方向转为时间上的「后来、随后、事后」；同族词另有 forward、toward。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of afterward all turn the mind towards what lies behind: later time, the next item in order, and looking back after the fact.
sensesIntro.cn: afterward 的三个义项都把心思转向后方：较晚的时间、顺序中的下一项，以及事后的回望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door closes behind an event and a person turns towards it later.
core.cn: 核心意象：事件之后门关上，人过一会儿才转向那扇门。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: the turn towards what is behind becomes a later time.
branches.cn: 时间线：朝后方转向，变成较晚的时间。

branches.en: THE SEQUENCE: the same turn becomes the next item in order.
branches.cn: 顺序线：同一次转向变成次序中的下一项。

branches.en: THE RETROSPECT: looking back after the fact is the mind doing the same turn.
branches.cn: 回顾线：事后回望就是心思做出同一次转向。

branches.en: THE CORE: whether counting time or reflecting, the direction stays the same.
branches.cn: 核心线：无论是计时还是反思，方向都保持不变。

branches.en: THE NARRATIVE: a story can move to the next step and then look back on it.
branches.cn: 叙事线：故事可以先走到下一步，再回头审视它。

intro.en: Afterward is after plus a very old suffix; the British variant adds one more ending.
intro.cn: afterward 是 after 加一个非常古老的后缀；英式变体又多一个词尾。

latinIntro.en: Afterward is Germanic in origin and has no Latin cognate, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: afterward 源自日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁同族一栏留空。

items.meaning: a closing section of a book

items.example: It is the older spelling of -ward.
items.exampleCN: 它是 -ward 更古老的拼写。

definition_zh: 再一次；又；回到原处；此外；反复；另一方面
definition_en: one more time, back to a former state, or in phrases adding a further point or repeating an action
core_image: 转过身，再朝同一个方向走一遍
scene: 炉子上的水凉了，客人还没到，主人把壶重新放回火上。She read the letter again and folded it away.
sceneCN: 这里 again 是「再一次」（第 1 个义项：同一个动作再做一遍）；句意为她把那封信又读了一遍，然后折好收起。

pos.zh: 副词：再一次；又；回到原处；此外；反复

derivatives.zh: 由 again 加副词属格 -es 构成，义为「反对；倚靠」，语义从「朝向、相对」偏移为「对抗」
由本词重叠构成，义为「反复地」，语义从「再一次」偏移为「一次又一次没有停歇」

senses.title: One more time
senses.definition: used to say that an action or event happens one more time
senses.definitionCN: 表示某个动作或事件再发生一次
senses.example: She read the letter again and folded it away.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那封信又读了一遍，然后折好收起。
senses.why: Old English ongean meant 'towards, opposite'; doing something again is turning back towards the same action for another pass.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ongean 意为「朝向、相对」，再做一次就是转回同一个动作、再走一遍。

senses.title: Back to a former place or state
senses.definition: used with verbs of returning to mean back to the place or condition one was in before
senses.definitionCN: 与表示返回的动词连用，指回到从前所在的地方或状态
senses.example: The tide came in and the boat was home again.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水涨起，船又回到了家。
senses.why: If again means a turn back towards something, then returning home or recovering health is that turn completed.
senses.whyCN: 既然 again 意为「转回某处」，那么回家或康复就是这一次转身的完成。

senses.title: Moreover, as a further point
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to add a further point in an argument
senses.definitionCN: 用在句首，在论述中补充另一个要点
senses.example: Again, the cost is the main problem.
senses.exampleCN: 再者，费用才是主要问题。
senses.why: The speaker turns back to the topic once more to add a point, so the repetition marker becomes a word for addition.
senses.whyCN: 说话人再一次转回话题补充一点，于是这个表示重复的标记就变成了表示「此外」的词。

senses.title: Repeatedly, over and over
senses.definition: used in the phrase again and again to mean repeatedly and without stopping
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 again and again，表示反复地、不停地
senses.example: He tried again and again before the lock opened.
senses.exampleCN: 他试了一次又一次，锁才打开。
senses.why: Doubling the word doubles the turn: one return after another becomes endless repetition.
senses.whyCN: 把这个词叠起来，就是一次次重复转身：一次接一次的返回变成无尽的反复。

senses.title: Then again: on the other hand
senses.definition: used in the phrase then again to introduce a contrasting or qualifying thought
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 then again，引出相反或补充的想法
senses.example: Then again, maybe she was right.
senses.exampleCN: 话说回来，也许她是对的。
senses.why: The mind turns back to the matter from another side, and that second turn is then again.
senses.whyCN: 心思从另一个侧面转回这件事，这第二次转身就是 then again。

intro.en: Again is a native Germanic adverb meaning 'towards, opposite', and it is the twin of against.
intro.cn: again 是本土日耳曼语副词，意为「朝向、相对」，与 against 是一对同源词。

items.en: A Germanic form meaning 'against, towards' is reconstructed; the exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语有一个表示「相对、朝向」的形式，确切形状不确定。

items.en: ongean meant 'towards, opposite, in return', and it was already used for repetition.
items.cn: ongean 意为「朝向、相对、回报」，当时已用于表示重复。

items.en: The form simplified to again, and the repetition sense became central.
items.cn: 形式简化为 again，重复义成为核心。

items.en: The adverb appeared in phrases such as again and again and once again.
items.cn: 这个副词出现在 again and again 与 once again 这类短语中。

items.en: Again added the additive use (again, there is the cost) and the phrase then again.
items.cn: again 又发展出补充用法（again, there is the cost）与短语 then again。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same 'against' root; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of repetition.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「相对」词根的词；近义组收表示重复的副词。

entries.definition: A preposition meaning opposed to or touching for support, from the same root as again.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「反对」或「倚靠」，与 again 同根。

entries.definition: A formal verb meaning to deny or contradict, built on the old 'against' root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「否认、反驳」，由古老的「相对」词根构成，属正式用语。

entries.definition: A dialect or nonstandard form of against, still heard in some regions.
entries.definitionCN: against 的方言或非标准形式，在一些地区仍能听到。

entries.definition: Once more, often in a fresh way; more literary than again.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「重新、再一次」，常带「以新的方式」之意，比 again 更书面。

entries.definition: Again from the beginning, in a new way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「重新、从头再来」。

entries.definition: Many times over; close to the again-and-again sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「反复地」，与 again and again 义接近。

entries.definition: One further time; the simplest equivalent of the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「再一次」，是第一义最简单的对应说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English form and the phrases again actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的古英语形式，以及 again 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: ongean meant towards or opposite: again is a turn back for another pass.
normal.cn: ongean 意为「朝向、相对」：again 就是转回去再走一遍。

normal.en: Again and against are twins from the same root.
normal.cn: again 与 against 是同根的一对双胞胎。

normal.en: Back again uses the original 'towards' picture: turning back to a place.
normal.cn: back again 用的是最初的「朝向」画面：转回某个地方。

normal.en: Again and again doubles the turn into endless repetition.
normal.cn: again and again 把转身叠成无尽的反复。

normal.en: Then again turns back to the matter from another side.
normal.cn: then again 是从另一个侧面转回这件事。

abstract.en: Picture a runner who turns around and runs the same stretch a second time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑步的人转过身，把同一段路再跑一遍。

abstract.en: The second run can end at home, can be repeated ten times, or can be a fresh look at the same problem.
abstract.cn: 这第二趟可以跑回家，可以重复十次，也可以是对同一个问题的新一轮审视。

abstract.en: Every use keeps one small turn: the mind goes back towards what it has already met.
abstract.cn: 每种用法都保留一次小小的转身：心思转回它已经遇见过的东西。

examples.en: Please say that again more slowly.
examples.cn: 请把那个再说一遍，慢一点。

examples.en: After a long walk they were glad to be home again.
examples.cn: 走了很久之后，他们很高兴又回到了家。

examples.en: Again, we must ask who pays for all this.
examples.cn: 再者，我们必须问一问这些费用由谁承担。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额根」——脚跟在后面一蹬，转回去再走一遍：再一次

root: 古英语 ongean「朝向、相对、回报」属日耳曼语副词，与 against 同源。词义由空间上的「相对、转回」发展出「再一次、回到原状」，再引申为「此外」与 then again 这类转折用法。更早的日耳曼语形式不确定，拉丁语中没有同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of again all contain one turn back: a second try, a return home, a further point, endless repetition, and a look from the other side.
sensesIntro.cn: again 的五个义项都含有一次转身：再试一遍、回到原处、补充一点、无尽重复，以及从另一面看问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner turns around and runs the same stretch a second time.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑步的人转过身，把同一段路再跑一遍。

branches.en: THE SECOND PASS: the same action is performed one more time.
branches.cn: 重做线：同一个动作再做一次。

branches.en: THE RETURN: the turn ends at the place or state one came from.
branches.cn: 返回线：这一次转身结束于原来的地方或状态。

branches.en: THE ADDITION: turning back to the topic adds a further point.
branches.cn: 补充线：转回话题，补充另一个要点。

branches.en: THE LOOP: repeated turns become again and again.
branches.cn: 循环线：一次次转身变成 again and again。

branches.en: THE OTHER SIDE: the second turn is taken from a contrasting angle.
branches.cn: 另一面线：第二次转身从相反的角度出发。

intro.en: Again is a native English adverb; its parts are a Germanic prefix and root still visible in against.
intro.cn: again 是本土英语副词，其成分是仍能在 against 中看见的日耳曼语前缀与词根。

latinIntro.en: Again is Germanic and has no Latin cognate, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: again 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁同族一栏留空。

items.example: It is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: 它是最早有记录的形式。

items.example: She came again the next day.

items.exampleCN: 它构成 againes，后来成为 against。

definition_zh: 反对；倚靠；违反；对抗；以防；以……为背景
definition_en: in opposition to something, touching something for support, contrary to a rule, or used as a defence or a background comparison
core_image: 身体或立场顶住另一面，正面相对
scene: 雨夜的小巷里，一个醉汉摇摇晃晃地推搡路边的木栅栏，栅栏被压得吱吱作响。He leaned against the wooden fence and would not move.
sceneCN: 这里 against 是「倚靠、紧靠」（第 2 个义项：身体贴着某物以获得支撑）；句意为他倚着木栅栏，不肯走开。

pos.zh: 介词：反对；倚靠；违反；对抗；以防；以……为背景

derivatives.zh: 与本词同出古英语 ongean 的副词，义为「再一次」，语义从「相对」偏移为「重复」
由古老的 gain-「反对」与 say 复合，义为「否认；反驳」，语义从「相对而言」偏移为「出言相抗」

senses.title: Opposed to something
senses.definition: in opposition to a person, plan, idea or action
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某计划、某想法或某行动持反对立场
senses.example: Most of the village voted against the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 村里大多数人投票反对这条新路。
senses.why: The core picture is two sides standing face to face; one side turned towards the other in resistance is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是两面相对而立；一面朝另一面顶过去、表示抗拒，就是第一义。

senses.title: Touching something for support
senses.definition: resting on or touching something so that it gives support
senses.definitionCN: 靠在或贴着某物，以便获得支撑
senses.example: He leaned against the wooden fence and would not move.
senses.exampleCN: 他倚着木栅栏，不肯走开。
senses.why: A body that leans on a wall presses its weight towards that surface, which is the same face-to-face contact.
senses.whyCN: 身体靠墙时把重量压向那个表面，正是同一种正面相抵的接触。

senses.title: Contrary to a rule or standard
senses.definition: not in agreement with a law, rule or principle
senses.definitionCN: 与法律、规则或原则不一致
senses.example: Driving without a licence is against the law.
senses.exampleCN: 无照驾驶是违法的。
senses.why: A rule is a line drawn in one direction, and an act that meets it head-on is against it.
senses.whyCN: 规则是一条划定的方向线，迎面撞上这条线的行为就是 against it。

senses.title: In a fight or struggle with something
senses.definition: used after verbs of fighting or competing to name the opponent
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示战斗或竞争的动词之后，引出对手
senses.example: The small team fought against a much larger company.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小团队与一家大得多的公司对抗。
senses.why: Two forces pushing towards each other is the original face-to-face picture at its most physical.
senses.whyCN: 两股力量彼此对推，正是最初「面对面」画面最物理的形态。

senses.title: As a defence or protection from
senses.definition: used to name the harm or danger that something is meant to prevent
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出某物所要防止的伤害或危险
senses.example: They stored extra wood against the cold winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们多存了些木柴，以防寒冬。
senses.why: A defence is a surface set up to face the coming danger, so what it faces is what it is against.
senses.whyCN: 防御是一面立起来迎向危险的墙，它迎向的东西就是它所防的东西。

senses.title: Compared with a background
senses.definition: used to show the background or standard by which something is seen or judged
senses.definitionCN: 用于表明观察或评判某物时所依托的背景或标准
senses.example: The white church stood out against the dark hills.
senses.exampleCN: 白色的教堂在深色山丘的衬托下十分醒目。
senses.why: One thing is placed in front of another so that the eye can compare them, and that contrast is against.
senses.whyCN: 一物被放在另一物前面，让眼睛比较二者，这种对照就是 against。

intro.en: Against is again plus an old genitive ending, and the two words still sit side by side in meaning.
intro.cn: against 是 again 加一个古老的所有格词尾，两个词在意义上至今并肩而立。

items.en: ongean meant 'towards, opposite, in return', the common ancestor of again and against.
items.cn: ongean 意为「朝向、相对、回报」，是 again 与 against 的共同祖先。

items.en: The form againes added an adverbial genitive -es to again.
items.cn: againes 这一形式在 again 之后加了副词性属格词尾 -es。

items.en: The final -st appeared by analogy with superlative and superlative-like forms, and the spelling settled.
items.cn: 词尾 -st 受最高级一类形式的类推而出现，拼写逐渐固定。

items.en: The preposition took over the opposition sense while again kept repetition.
items.cn: 这个介词承担了「相对、反对」义，again 则保留重复义。

items.en: Against extended to defence, support and background comparison.
items.cn: against 又扩展到防御、倚靠与背景对比。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same ongean root; the near-meaning group gathers prepositions of opposition and position.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 ongean 词根的词；近义组收表示对立与位置的介词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning one more time; the twin that kept the repetition sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「再一次」，是保留重复义的同源双胞胎。

entries.definition: A formal verb meaning to contradict or deny, built on the old 'against' element.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「反驳、否认」，由古老的「反对」成分构成，属正式用语。

entries.definition: A dialect or nonstandard form of against.
entries.definitionCN: against 的方言或非标准形式。

entries.definition: Against, especially in a contest or legal case; more formal and often written as v.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「对、与……相对」，多用于比赛或法律案件，较正式。

entries.definition: Facing something on the other side; the positional cousin of against.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或形容词，义为「在……对面」，是 against 位置义的近亲。

entries.definition: Next to or at the side of something; close to the support sense.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……旁边」，与「倚靠」义接近。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning against or opposed to, as in anti-war.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀，义为「反对、抵抗」，如 anti-war 中的用法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English root and the phrases against actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的古英语词根，以及 against 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: ongean means opposite: against is the word for standing face to face.
normal.cn: ongean 意为「相对」：against 就是面对面站着的那个词。

normal.en: again and against are twins: one kept repetition, one kept opposition.
normal.cn: again 与 against 是双胞胎：一个保留重复，一个保留对立。

normal.en: Against the law names the rule that one act meets head-on.
normal.cn: against the law 指的是被某个行为迎面撞上的规则。

normal.en: Protect against names the danger a defence faces.
normal.cn: protect against 引出防御所面对的危险。

normal.en: Against a background places one thing in front of another for comparison.
normal.cn: against a background 把一物放到另一物前面作对比。

abstract.en: Picture two doors facing each other, each pressing on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇门正面相对，各自向对方压过去。

abstract.en: The same facing can be a fight, a rule being broken, a body leaning for support, or a wall built to stop the cold.
abstract.cn: 同一种相对可以是打斗、被违反的规则、寻求支撑的身体，或挡住寒风的墙。

abstract.en: Sometimes one object is simply placed before another so the eye can measure the difference.
abstract.cn: 有时只是一物被放在另一物前面，让眼睛去衡量差别。

examples.en: Many parents argued against the longer school day.
examples.cn: 许多家长反对延长在校时间。

examples.en: She put the ladder against the wall.
examples.cn: 她把梯子靠在墙上。

examples.en: The village looks small against the huge mountains.
examples.cn: 在巨大的群山映衬下，这个村庄显得很小。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额根斯特」——额头一顶，正面顶住对方：反对、倚靠

root: 中古英语 againes 来自古英语 ongean「朝向、相对」，在 again 之后加副词性属格词尾 -es，词尾后又受类推出现 -st，成为 against。词义由「面对面」发展出「反对、对抗、违反、倚靠、以防、对比」；与 again 同源，拉丁语中没有同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of against all keep two things facing each other: opposition, support, a broken rule, a fight, a defence, and a background for comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: against 的六个义项都保留两物相对：反对、倚靠、违反规则、对抗、防御，以及作为比较的背景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two doors face each other and press together.
core.cn: 核心意象：两扇门正面相对，彼此压在一起。

branches.en: THE OPPOSITION: facing the other side becomes argument or open struggle.
branches.cn: 对立线：正面相对变成争论或公开的斗争。

branches.en: THE CONTACT: pressing towards a surface becomes leaning for support.
branches.cn: 接触线：朝表面压过去，变成倚靠求支撑。

branches.en: THE RULE: an act that meets a rule head-on violates it.
branches.cn: 规则线：迎面撞上规则的行为就是违反它。

branches.en: THE DEFENCE: a wall faces the danger it is meant to stop.
branches.cn: 防御线：一面墙迎向它要挡住的危险。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: one thing is set before another so the eye can compare.
branches.cn: 对比线：一物被放在另一物前面，让眼睛比较。

intro.en: Against is a native word; its endings are historical, and the same root still shows in again and gainsay.
intro.cn: against 是本土词，其词尾属历史沉积，同一词根仍见于 again 与 gainsay。

latinIntro.en: Against is Germanic and has no Latin cognate, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: against 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁同族一栏留空。

items.example: It is the core of ongean.
It is the common ancestor of two words.
items.exampleCN: 它是两个词的共同祖先。
